sentences.zh: 卷第一百八

translations.literal: Volume 108
translations.idiomatic: Volume 108

sentences.zh: 【晉紀三十】起玄黓執徐，盡柔兆涒灘，凡五年。

translations.literal: 【Jin Records 30】 From Xuanxi Zhichen through Rouzhao Tuotan—in all, five years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Jin Records 30】 From the first year of the Xuanxi cycle through the last year of the Rouzhao cycle—five years in all.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝下太元十七年

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong, the seventeenth year of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong: the seventeenth year of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，已巳朔，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the jisi new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the jisi new moon, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 秦主登立昭儀隴西李氏為皇后。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng installed the Zhaoyi Lady Li of Longxi as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Qin ruler Yao Deng made Lady Li of Longxi, his Zhaoyi, empress.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬寅，燕主垂自魯口如河間、渤海、平原。

translations.literal: In the second month, on renyin, the Yan ruler Chui went from Lukou toward Hejian, Bohai, and Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renyin, Murong Chui of Yan traveled from Lukou through Hejian, Bohai, and Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 翟釗遣其將翟都侵館陶，屯蘇康壘。

translations.literal: Zhai Zhao sent his general Zhai Du to raid Guantao and encamped at Sukang stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Zhao sent his general Zhai Du to raid Guantao and camp at Sukang Fort.

sentences.zh: 三月，垂引兵南擊釗。

translations.literal: In the third month, Chui led troops south to attack Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Chui marched south against Zhai Zhao.

sentences.zh: 秦驃騎將軍沒弈干帥眾降於後秦，後秦以為車騎將軍，封高平公。

translations.literal: Qin's General of Agile Cavalry Moyigan led his hosts to surrender to Later Qin; Later Qin made him General of Chariots and Cavalry and enfeoffed him as Duke of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Qin General of Agile Cavalry Moyigan surrendered with his forces to Later Qin, which appointed him General of Chariots and Cavalry and created him Duke of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇寢疾，命姚碩德鎮李潤，尹緯守長安，召太子興詣行營。

translations.literal: The Later Qin ruler Chang fell ill in bed and ordered Yao Shuode to guard Lirun, Yin Wei to hold Chang'an, and summoned the crown prince Xing to the campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin ruler Yao Chang took to his bed. He ordered Yao Shuode to hold Lirun, Yin Wei to defend Chang'an, and summoned Crown Prince Yao Xing to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 征南將軍姚方成言於興曰：「今寇敵未滅，上復寢疾。

translations.literal: The General Who Conquers the South Yao Fangcheng said to Xing: "Now the enemy bandits are not yet destroyed, and Our Lord is again ill in bed.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the South Yao Fangcheng told Xing, "The enemy is not yet destroyed, and the emperor is ill again.

sentences.zh: 王統等皆有部曲，終為人患，宜盡除之。」

translations.literal: Wang Tong and the others all have private followings; in the end they will become a menace to others. They ought all to be eliminated."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong and the others all command private bands—they will become a threat in time. You should eliminate them all."

sentences.zh: 興從之，殺王統、王廣、苻胤、徐成、毛盛。

translations.literal: Xing followed this advice and killed Wang Tong, Wang Guang, Fu Yin, Xu Cheng, and Mao Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xing agreed and had Wang Tong, Wang Guang, Fu Yin, Xu Cheng, and Mao Sheng put to death.

sentences.zh: 萇怒曰：「王統兄弟，吾之州裡，實無他志；

translations.literal: Chang said in anger: "The Wang brothers are men of my native district and truly had no other designs;
translations.idiomatic: Chang raged, "The Wang brothers are men from my home district and had no other designs;

sentences.zh: 徐成等皆前朝名將，吾方用之，奈何輒殺之！」

translations.literal: Xu Cheng and the rest are all famous generals of the former dynasty—I was just about to employ them. How could you kill them outright!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Cheng and the rest are famous generals of the former court—I was about to put them to use. How could you kill them out of hand!"

sentences.zh: 燕主垂進逼蘇康壘。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Chui pressed forward against Sukang stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui pressed on Sukang Fort.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，翟都南走滑台。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Zhai Du fled south to Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Zhai Du fled south to Huatai.

sentences.zh: 翟釗求救於西燕，西燕主永謀於群臣，尚書渤海鮑遵曰：「使兩寇相弊，吾承其後，此卞莊子之策也。」

translations.literal: Zhai Zhao sought rescue from Western Yan. The Western Yan ruler Yong consulted his ministers. Bao Zun of Bohai, Director of the Masters of Writing, said: "Let the two marauders wear each other down; we take them afterward—this is the stratagem of Bian Zhuangzi."
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Zhao appealed to Western Yan for help. Murong Yong consulted his ministers. Bao Zun of Bohai, Director of the Masters of Writing, said, "Let the two foes wear each other down, then we strike afterward—this is Bian Zhuangzi's stratagem."

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎太原張騰曰：「垂強釗弱，何弊之承！

translations.literal: Zhang Teng of Taiyuan, Gentleman Attendant of the Masters of Writing, said: "Chui is strong and Zhao weak—what wearing-down is there to reap!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Teng of Taiyuan, Gentleman Attendant of the Masters of Writing, said, "Chui is strong and Zhao weak—what exhaustion is there to harvest!

sentences.zh: 不如速救之，以成鼎足之勢。

translations.literal: Better to rescue him at once and complete the tripod stance.
translations.idiomatic: Better to rescue him at once and secure a tripod balance of power.

sentences.zh: 今我引兵趨中山，晝多疑兵，夜多火炬，垂必懼而自救。

translations.literal: If we now lead troops toward Zhongshan, by day deploying many doubtful detachments and by night many torches, Chui will surely fear and come to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: If we march on Zhongshan now, feigning large forces by day and lighting many torches by night, Chui will surely turn back in alarm to save himself.

sentences.zh: 我沖其前，釗躡其後，此天授之機，不可失也。」

translations.literal: We strike him in front and Zhao follows at his rear—this is a heaven-sent opportunity and must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: We strike from the front while Zhao closes on his rear—this is heaven's gift and must not be missed."

sentences.zh: 永不從。

translations.literal: Yong would not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Yong refused.

sentences.zh: 燕大赦。

translations.literal: Yan proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yan proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the dingmao new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the dingmao new moon, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 六月，燕主垂軍黎陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Yan ruler Chui encamped at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Murong Chui encamped at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 臨河欲濟，翟釗列兵南岸以拒之。

translations.literal: Facing the river and wishing to cross, Zhai Zhao arrayed troops on the south bank to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: As he came to the river intending to cross, Zhai Zhao drew up his army on the south bank to block him.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，垂徙營就西津，去黎陽西四十里，為牛皮船百餘艘，偽列兵仗，溯流而上。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Chui moved camp to Xijin, forty li west of Liyang, made more than a hundred oxhide boats, falsely arrayed arms and armor, and went upstream.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Chui shifted camp to Xijin, forty li west of Liyang, built more than a hundred oxhide boats, displayed arms and armor as a feint, and moved upstream.

sentences.zh: 釗亟引兵趣西津，垂潛遣中壘將軍桂林王鎮等自黎陽津夜濟，營於河南，比明而營成。

translations.literal: Zhao hurriedly led troops toward Xijin. Chui secretly sent the General of the Central Ramparts, Murong Zhen of Guilin, and others to cross by night from Liyang Ford; they encamped south of the river, and by dawn the camp was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao rushed his army toward Xijin. Chui secretly sent General of the Central Ramparts Murong Zhen of Guilin and others to cross at night from Liyang Ford and encamp south of the river; by dawn the camp was finished.

sentences.zh: 釗聞之，亟還，攻鎮等營；

translations.literal: When Zhao heard of this, he hurried back and attacked Zhen's camp;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao heard of this, he hurried back and assaulted Zhen's camp;

sentences.zh: 垂命鎮等堅壁勿戰。

translations.literal: Chui ordered Zhen and the others to hold the walls and not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chui ordered Zhen and the others to hold the walls and not fight.

sentences.zh: 釗兵往來疲暍，攻營不能拔，將引去；

translations.literal: Zhao's troops, going back and forth, grew weary and exhausted; they could not take the camp and were about to withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's men, shuttling back and forth, grew exhausted; they could not storm the camp and were about to withdraw;

sentences.zh: 鎮等引兵出戰。

translations.literal: Zhen and the others led troops out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and the others sallied out to fight.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍農自西津濟，與鎮等夾擊，大破之。

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry Nong crossed from Xijin and, with Zhen and the others attacking from both sides, routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: General of Agile Cavalry Murong Nong crossed from Xijin and, with Zhen attacking from the other side, crushed them.

sentences.zh: 釗走還滑台，將妻子，收遺眾，北濟河，登白鹿山，憑險自守，燕兵不得進。

translations.literal: Zhao fled back to Huatai, took wife and children, gathered the scattered host, crossed the river north, ascended Bailu Mountain, and relied on the terrain to hold himself; Yan troops could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao fled to Huatai, took his family, gathered the remnants, crossed north over the river, and held Bailu Mountain's defiles; Yan troops could not press him.

sentences.zh: 農曰：「釗無糧，不能久居山中。」

translations.literal: Nong said: "Zhao has no grain and cannot long remain in the mountains."
translations.idiomatic: Nong said, "Zhao has no grain—he cannot stay long in the hills."

sentences.zh: 乃引兵還，留騎候之。

translations.literal: He then led the army back, leaving cavalry to watch for him.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew, leaving cavalry to watch for him.

sentences.zh: 釗果下山；

translations.literal: Zhao did indeed come down the mountain;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao did come down the mountain;

sentences.zh: 還兵掩擊，盡獲其眾，釗單騎奔長子。

translations.literal: the returning troops fell on him by surprise, captured his entire host, and Zhao alone on horseback fled to Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: the waiting troops struck and took his whole force; Zhao alone fled on horseback to Changzi.

sentences.zh: 西燕主永以釗為車騎大將軍、兗州牧，封東郡王。

translations.literal: The Western Yan ruler Yong made Zhao General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Yanzhou, enfeoffing him as King of Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong made Zhao General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Yanzhou, creating him King of Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，釗謀反，永殺之。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Zhao plotted rebellion and Yong killed him.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Zhao plotted rebellion, and Yong had him killed.

sentences.zh: 初，郝晷、崔逞及清河崔宏、新興張卓、遼東夔騰、陽平路纂皆仕於秦，避秦亂來奔，詔以為冀州諸郡，各將部曲營於河南。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hao Chao, Cui Cheng, Cui Hong of Qinghe, Zhang Zhuo of Xingxing, Kui Teng of Liaodong, and Lu Zuan of Yangping had all served Qin; fleeing Qin's turmoil they came to submit, and an edict made them chiefs of the various commanderies of Jizhou, each leading his private following to encamp south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hao Chao, Cui Cheng, Cui Hong of Qinghe, Zhang Zhuo of Xingxing, Kui Teng of Liaodong, and Lu Zuan of Yangping had all served Qin. Fleeing its chaos they submitted to Jin, and the court assigned them Jizhou commanderies, each leading his band to camp south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 既而受翟氏官爵，翟氏敗，皆降於燕，燕主垂各隨其材而用之。

translations.literal: Later they accepted offices and ranks from the Zhai clan; when the Zhai clan was defeated they all surrendered to Yan, and the Yan ruler Chui employed each according to his talent.
translations.idiomatic: They later accepted offices from the Zhai clan; when the Zhai fell they all surrendered to Yan, and Murong Chui employed each according to his ability.

sentences.zh: 釗所統七郡三萬餘戶，皆按堵如故。

translations.literal: The seven commanderies and more than thirty thousand households that Zhao had ruled all remained settled as before.
translations.idiomatic: The seven commanderies and more than thirty thousand households under Zhao remained undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 以章武王宙為兗、豫二州刺史，鎮滑台；

translations.literal: He made Murong Zhou, Prince of Zhangwu, Governor of Yan and Yu provinces and stationed him at Huatai;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Murong Zhou, Prince of Zhangwu, Governor of Yan and Yu provinces and stationed him at Huatai;

sentences.zh: 徙徐州民七千餘戶於黎陽，以彭城王脫為徐州刺史，鎮黎陽。

translations.literal: he moved more than seven thousand households of Xuzhou to Liyang, and made Murong Tuo, Prince of Pengcheng, Governor of Xuzhou, stationed at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: moved more than seven thousand households from Xuzhou to Liyang, and made Murong Tuo, Prince of Pengcheng, Governor of Xuzhou at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 脫，垂之弟子也。

translations.literal: Tuo was Chui's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo was Chui's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 垂以崔廕為宙司馬。

translations.literal: Chui made Cui Yin Zhou's Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Chui made Cui Yin Chief Clerk to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 初，陳留王紹為鎮南將軍，太原王楷為征西將軍，樂浪王溫為征東將軍，垂皆以廕為之佐。

translations.literal: Earlier, Murong Shao, Prince of Chenliu, was General Who Guards the South; Murong Kai, Prince of Taiyuan, was General Who Conquers the West; Murong Wen, Prince of Lelang, was General Who Conquers the East—and Chui had made Yin assistant to each.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Murong Shao of Chenliu had been General Who Guards the South, Murong Kai of Taiyuan General Who Conquers the West, and Murong Wen of Lelang General Who Conquers the East—and Chui had placed Yin as aide to each.

sentences.zh: 廕才幹明敏強正，善規諫，四王皆嚴憚之；

translations.literal: Yin was talented, keen, forceful, and upright, skilled at remonstrance; the four princes all stood in awe of him;
translations.idiomatic: Yin was capable, sharp, upright, and skilled at remonstrance; all four princes stood in awe of him;

sentences.zh: 所至簡刑法，輕賦役，流民歸之，戶口滋息。

translations.literal: wherever he went he simplified penal law and lightened levies and corvée; displaced people returned to him and households multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: wherever he served he simplified penal law and eased taxes and labor; refugees returned and the population grew.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，垂如鄴，以太原王楷為冀州牧，右光祿大夫餘蔚為左僕射。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Chui went to Ye and made Murong Kai, Prince of Taiyuan, Governor of Jizhou, and Yu Wei, Grandee of Splendid Happiness on the Right, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Chui went to Ye, made Murong Kai of Taiyuan Governor of Jizhou, and Yu Wei, Grandee of Splendid Happiness on the Right, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 秦主登聞後秦主萇疾病，大喜，告祠世祖神主，大赦，百官進位二等，秣馬厲兵，進逼安定，去城九十餘里。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng heard that the Later Qin ruler Chang was ill and was greatly pleased. He reported to the ancestral tablets of Emperor Shizu, proclaimed a general amnesty, advanced all officials two ranks, foddered horses and sharpened weapons, and pressed toward Anding, coming within more than ninety li of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Qin ruler Yao Deng heard that Yao Chang of Later Qin was ill and rejoiced. He reported to the ancestral tablets of Emperor Shizu, proclaimed a general amnesty, raised all officials two ranks, readied horses and arms, and marched on Anding until he was within ninety li of the city.

sentences.zh: 八月，萇疾小瘳，出拒之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Chang's illness eased somewhat and he went out to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Chang's illness eased, and he went out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 登引兵出營，將逆戰，萇遣安南將軍姚熙隆別攻秦營，登懼而還。

translations.literal: Deng led troops out of camp intending to give battle head-on; Chang sent the General Who Pacifies the South Yao Xilong to attack the Qin camp separately, and Deng, in fear, returned.
translations.idiomatic: Deng led his army out to give battle; Chang sent General Who Pacifies the South Yao Xilong to strike the Qin camp from another direction, and Deng withdrew in alarm.

sentences.zh: 萇夜引兵旁出以躡其後，旦而候騎告曰：「賊諸營已空，不知所向。」

translations.literal: Chang by night led troops out by a side route to follow on Deng's rear. At dawn the scouts reported: "The bandits' camps are all empty; we do not know where they have gone."
translations.idiomatic: Chang marched out by night on a flank route to fall on Deng's rear. At dawn scouts reported, "The enemy camps are empty—we do not know where they have gone."

sentences.zh: 登驚曰：「彼為何人，去令我不知，來令我不覺，謂其將死，忽然復來，朕與此羌同世，何其厄哉！」

translations.literal: Deng said in alarm: "What manner of man is he—when he leaves I do not know it, when he comes I do not perceive it! I thought he was about to die, yet suddenly he is back again. I share this age with this Qiang—how bitter is my fate!"
translations.idiomatic: Deng cried in alarm, "What sort of man is he—when he leaves I never know, when he comes I never see him! I thought he was dying, yet suddenly he is back. To share an age with this Qiang—what bitter fate!"

sentences.zh: 登遂還雍，萇亦還安定。

translations.literal: Deng then returned to Yong, and Chang also returned to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Deng withdrew to Yong, and Chang returned to Anding.

sentences.zh: 三河王光遣其弟右將軍寶等攻金城王乾歸，寶及將士死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Lü Guang, King of Sanhe, sent his younger brother the Right General Bao and others to attack Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng; Bao and officers and soldiers who died numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang, King of Sanhe, sent his younger brother Right General Bao and others against Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng; Bao and more than ten thousand officers and men were killed.

sentences.zh: 又遣其子虎賁中郎將纂擊南羌彭奚念，纂亦敗歸。

translations.literal: He also sent his son Zuan, Tiger Guard Commandant of the Gentlemen of the Palace, to attack the Southern Qiang Peng Xinian; Zuan too was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his son Zuan, Tiger Guard Commandant of the Gentlemen of the Palace, against the Southern Qiang Peng Xinian; Zuan too was beaten and retreated.

sentences.zh: 光自將擊奚念於枹罕，克之，奚念奔甘松。

translations.literal: Guang himself led troops to attack Xinian at Fuhan, took it, and Xinian fled to Gansong.
translations.idiomatic: Guang led the army himself against Xinian at Fuhan, took the place, and Xinian fled to Gansong.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛亥，荊州刺史王忱卒。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinhai, Wang Chen, Governor of Jingzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on xinhai, Wang Chen, Governor of Jingzhou, died.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史朱序以老病求解職，詔以太子右衛率郗恢為雍州刺史，代序鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Zhu Xu, Governor of Yongzhou, because of age and illness requested to be relieved of office; an edict made Xi Hui, Leader of the Right Guards of the Heir Apparent, Governor of Yongzhou to replace Xu and guard Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu, Governor of Yongzhou, asked to retire on account of age and illness. The court appointed Xi Hui, Leader of the Right Guards of the Heir Apparent, Governor of Yongzhou in his place to guard Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 恢，曇之子也。

translations.literal: Hui was the son of Xi Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was the son of Xi Tan.

sentences.zh: 巴蜀人在關中者皆叛後秦，據弘農以附秦。

translations.literal: All Ba-Shu people in Guanzhong rebelled against Later Qin, seized Hongnong, and attached themselves to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Ba-Shu people throughout Guanzhong rebelled against Later Qin, seized Hongnong, and submitted to Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦主登以竇沖為左丞相，沖徙屯華陰。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng made Dou Chong Left Chancellor; Chong moved to encamp at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Qin ruler Yao Deng made Dou Chong Left Chancellor, and Chong encamped at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 郗恢遣將軍趙睦守金墉，河南太守楊佺期帥眾軍湖城，擊沖，走之。

translations.literal: Xi Hui sent the general Zhao Mu to hold Jinyong; Yang Quanqi, Administrator of Henan, led the host to Hucheng, attacked Chong, and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Hui sent General Zhao Mu to hold Jinyong; Yang Quanqi, Administrator of Henan, led troops to Hucheng, attacked Chong, and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸酉，以黃門郎殷仲堪為都督荊、益、寧三州諸軍事、荊州刺史，鎮江陵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on guiyou, Yin Zhongkan, Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, was made Supervisor of Military Affairs for Jing, Yi, and Ning provinces and Governor of Jingzhou, stationed at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on guiyou, Yin Zhongkan, Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, was made Supervisor of Military Affairs for Jing, Yi, and Ning provinces and Governor of Jingzhou at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 仲堪雖有英譽，資望猶淺，議者不以為允。

translations.literal: Although Zhongkan had a reputation for excellence, his seniority and standing were still shallow, and those who discussed the matter did not consider it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhongkan enjoyed a fine reputation, his seniority was slight, and critics thought the appointment ill advised.

sentences.zh: 到官，好行小惠，綱目不舉。

translations.literal: When he reached office he liked to dispense petty favors and did not uphold the main lines of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he dispensed petty favors and neglected the larger framework of rule.

sentences.zh: 南郡公桓玄負其才地，以雄豪自處，朝廷疑而不用。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan, Duke of Nanjun, relied on his talent and position and conducted himself as a bold hero; the court was suspicious and did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan, Duke of Nanjun, relied on his talent and birth and carried himself as a bold hero; the court mistrusted him and kept him idle.

sentences.zh: 年二十三，始拜太子洗馬。

translations.literal: At age twenty-three he was first appointed Groom in Attendance to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-three he was first appointed Groom in Attendance to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 玄嘗詣琅邪王道子，值其酣醉，張目謂眾客曰：「桓溫晚途欲作賊，雲何？」

translations.literal: Xuan once called on Sima Daozi, Prince of Langye; finding him deep in drink, Daozi opened his eyes wide and said to the assembled guests: "Huan Wen in his late years wished to play the rebel—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan once visited Sima Daozi, Prince of Langye, and found him drunk. Daozi glared at the guests and said, "Huan Wen in his last years meant to play the rebel—what of it?"

sentences.zh: 玄伏地流汗，不能起。

translations.literal: Xuan prostrated himself, sweating, and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan prostrated himself, streaming sweat, unable to rise.

sentences.zh: 由是益不自安，常切齒於道子。

translations.literal: From this he grew still more ill at ease and often gnashed his teeth at Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he grew still more uneasy and often gnashed his teeth at Daozi.

sentences.zh: 後出補義興太守，鬱鬱不得志，歎曰：「父為九州伯，兒為五湖長！」

translations.literal: Later he went out to fill the post of Administrator of Yixing, sullen and unfulfilled, and sighed: "My father was lord of the Nine Provinces, and I am chief of the Five Lakes!"
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posted as Administrator of Yixing, sullen and frustrated, and sighed, "My father was lord of the Nine Provinces, and I am chief of the Five Lakes!"

sentences.zh: 遂棄官歸國，上疏自訟曰：「先臣勤王匡復之勳，朝廷遺之，臣不復計。

translations.literal: He thereupon abandoned office and returned to the capital, memorializing in his own defense: "My late father served the royal house and restored the realm—if the court has forgotten that, I shall say no more.
translations.idiomatic: He quit his post and returned to the capital, memorializing in his own defense, "My late father's service in restoring the dynasty—the court may forget it; I shall say no more.

sentences.zh: 至於先帝龍飛，陛下繼明，請問談者，誰之由邪？」

translations.literal: As for the late emperor's ascent and Your Majesty's succession—may I ask those who talk, whose doing was that?"
translations.idiomatic: But when the late emperor ascended and Your Majesty succeeded—tell me, whose doing was that?"

sentences.zh: 疏寢不報。

translations.literal: The memorial lay dormant with no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 玄在江陵，仲堪甚敬憚之。

translations.literal: When Xuan was at Jiangling, Zhongkan greatly respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan was at Jiangling, Zhongkan treated him with great respect and fear.

sentences.zh: 桓氏累世臨荊州，玄復豪橫，士民畏之，過於仲堪。

translations.literal: The Huan clan had for generations governed Jingzhou; Xuan was again overbearing and domineering, and gentry and commoners feared him more than they did Zhongkan.
translations.idiomatic: The Huans had governed Jingzhou for generations; Xuan was domineering again, and officials and people feared him even more than Zhongkan.

sentences.zh: 嘗於仲堪聽事前戲馬，以槊擬仲堪。

translations.literal: Once before Zhongkan's audience hall he sported with a horse and pointed his lance at Zhongkan.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the courtyard before Zhongkan's hall he played with his horse and leveled his lance at Zhongkan.

sentences.zh: 仲堪中兵參軍彭城劉邁謂玄曰：「馬槊有餘，精理不足。」

translations.literal: Liu Mai of Pengcheng, Army Controller under Zhongkan, said to Xuan: "Your cavalry lance has surplus force, but refined principle falls short."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mai of Pengcheng, Army Controller under Zhongkan, told Xuan, "Your lance has force to spare, but your judgment falls short."

sentences.zh: 玄不悅，仲堪為之失色。

translations.literal: Xuan was displeased, and Zhongkan turned pale on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was displeased, and Zhongkan turned pale.

sentences.zh: 玄出，仲堪謂邁曰：「卿，狂人也！

translations.literal: When Xuan had gone out, Zhongkan said to Mai: "You are a madman!
translations.idiomatic: After Xuan left, Zhongkan said to Mai, "You are mad!

sentences.zh: 玄夜遣殺卿，我豈能相救邪？」

translations.literal: If Xuan sends men by night to kill you, how could I save you?"
translations.idiomatic: If Xuan sends men tonight to kill you, how could I save you?"

sentences.zh: 使邁下都避之；

translations.literal: He had Mai go down to the capital to avoid him;
translations.idiomatic: He sent Mai down to the capital to escape;

sentences.zh: 玄使人追之，邁僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Xuan sent men in pursuit, and Mai barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent men after him, and Mai barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 征虜參軍豫章胡籓過江陵，見仲堪，說之曰：「桓玄志趣不常，每怏怏於失職，節下崇待太守，恐非將來之計也！」

translations.literal: Hu Fan of Yuzhang, staff officer of the General Who Conquers the Barbarians, passed through Jiangling, saw Zhongkan, and urged him: "Huan Xuan's aims are not steady; he is always resentful at losing office. My lord honors and treats this Administrator too highly— I fear this is no plan for the future!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fan of Yuzhang, staff officer under the General Who Conquers the Barbarians, passed through Jiangling and warned Zhongkan, "Huan Xuan's aims are unstable and he resents his loss of office. You honor him too highly—this is no plan for the future!"

sentences.zh: 仲堪不悅。

translations.literal: Zhongkan was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan was displeased.

sentences.zh: 籓內弟同郡羅企生為仲堪功曹，籓退，謂企生曰：「殷侯倒戈以授人，必及於禍。

translations.literal: Fan's wife's brother Luo Qisheng of the same commandery was Zhongkan's Merit Officer. When Fan withdrew he said to Qisheng: "Lord Yin turns his blade over to hand it to another—he is sure to meet with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's brother-in-law Luo Qisheng of the same commandery served Zhongkan as Merit Officer. As Fan left he told Qisheng, "Lord Yin is handing his sword to another man—disaster is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 君不早圖去就，後悔無及矣！」

translations.literal: If you do not early plan whether to stay or go, later regret will be too late!"
translations.idiomatic: If you do not decide early whether to stay or go, you will regret it too late!"

sentences.zh: 庚寅，立皇子德文為琅邪王，徙琅邪王道子為會稽王。

translations.literal: On gengyin the prince Dewen was established as Prince of Langye, and Sima Daozi, Prince of Langye, was moved to Prince of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Prince Dewen was created Prince of Langye, and Sima Daozi was moved from Prince of Langye to Prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 十二月，燕主垂還中山，以遼西王農為都督兗、豫、荊、徐、雍五州諸軍事，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Yan ruler Chui returned to Zhongshan and made Murong Nong, Prince of Liaoxi, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Yan, Yu, Jing, Xu, and Yong provinces, stationed at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Murong Chui returned to Zhongshan and made Murong Nong, Prince of Liaoxi, Supervisor of Military Affairs for five provinces—Yan, Yu, Jing, Xu, and Yong—stationed at Ye.

sentences.zh: 休官權千成據顯親，自稱秦州牧。

translations.literal: Quan Qiancheng of Xiuguan seized Xianqin and styled himself Governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Qiancheng of Xiuguan seized Xianqin and declared himself Governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 清河人李遼上表請敕兗州修孔子廟，給戶灑掃，仍立庠序，收教學者，曰：「事有如賒而實急者，此之謂也！」

translations.literal: Li Liao of Qinghe submitted a memorial asking that an edict order Yanzhou to repair the temple of Confucius, supply households for sweeping, and also establish a school and gather students for instruction, saying: "There are matters that seem remote yet are in fact urgent—this is one!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Liao of Qinghe memorialized asking the court to order Yanzhou to repair Confucius's temple, assign households to maintain it, and establish a school to gather students, writing, "Some matters seem distant yet are urgent—this is one!"

sentences.zh: 表不見省。

translations.literal: The memorial was not examined.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unread.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝下太元十八年

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong, the eighteenth year of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong: the eighteenth year of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，燕陽平孝王柔卒。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Murong Rou, Prince of Yangping and posthumously styled Filial, died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Murong Rou, Prince of Yangping, died.

sentences.zh: 權千成為秦所逼，請降於金城王乾歸，乾歸以為東秦州刺史、休官大都統、顯親公。

translations.literal: Quan Qiancheng, pressed by Qin, asked to surrender to Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng; Gangui made him Governor of East Qinzhou, Grand Commander of Xiuguan, and Duke of Xianqin.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by Qin, Quan Qiancheng submitted to Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng, who made him Governor of East Qinzhou, Grand Commander of Xiuguan, and Duke of Xianqin.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚子，燕主垂加太子寶大單于；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on gengzi, the Yan ruler Chui advanced the crown prince Bao to Great Chanyu;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on gengzi, Murong Chui advanced Crown Prince Bao to Great Chanyu;

sentences.zh: 以安定王庫辱官偉為太尉，范陽王德為司徒，太原王楷為司空，陳留王紹為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: he made Murong Guanwei, Prince of Anding, Grand Commandant; Murong De, Prince of Fanyang, Minister over the Masses; Murong Kai, Prince of Taiyuan, Minister of Works; and Murong Shao, Prince of Chenliu, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: made Murong Guanwei of Anding Grand Commandant, Murong De of Fanyang Minister over the Masses, Murong Kai of Taiyuan Minister of Works, and Murong Shao of Chenliu Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 五月，立子熙為河間王，朗為渤海王，鑒為博陵王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he established his sons Xi as Prince of Hejian, Lang as Prince of Bohai, and Jian as Prince of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he created his sons Xi Prince of Hejian, Lang Prince of Bohai, and Jian Prince of Boling.

sentences.zh: 秦右丞相竇沖矜才尚人，自請封天水王，秦主登不許。

translations.literal: Dou Chong, Right Chancellor of Qin, prized his talent and esteemed himself above others; he asked on his own to be enfeoffed as King of Tianshui, and the Qin ruler Deng did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong, Qin's Right Chancellor, prized his talent and held himself above others; he asked to be created King of Tianshui, and Yao Deng refused.

sentences.zh: 六月，沖自稱秦王，改元元光。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Chong styled himself King of Qin and changed the era name to Yuanguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Chong declared himself King of Qin and adopted the era name Yuanguang.

sentences.zh: 金城王乾歸立其子熾磐為太子。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng, established his son Chipan as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng, made his son Chipan crown prince.

sentences.zh: 熾磐勇略明決，過於其父。

translations.literal: Chipan was brave, resourceful, clear, and decisive—surpassing his father.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan was brave, resourceful, and decisive—surpassing his father.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，秦主登攻竇沖於野人堡，沖求救於後秦。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Qin ruler Deng attacked Dou Chong at Yeren Fort; Chong sought rescue from Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Yao Deng attacked Dou Chong at Yeren Fort; Chong appealed to Later Qin for help.

sentences.zh: 尹緯言於後秦主萇曰：「太子仁厚之稱，著於遠近，而英略未著，請使擊苻以著之。」

translations.literal: Yin Wei said to the Later Qin ruler Chang: "The crown prince's reputation for kindness and generosity is known far and near, yet his heroic designs are not yet manifest. I ask that he be sent to attack the Fu clan so that they may be made manifest."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei told Yao Chang, "The crown prince's reputation for kindness is known far and wide, but his martial renown is not yet established. Send him against the Fu clan to establish it."

sentences.zh: 萇從之。

translations.literal: Chang followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Chang agreed.

sentences.zh: 太子興將兵攻胡空堡，登解沖圍以赴之。

translations.literal: The crown prince Xing led troops to attack Hukong Fort; Deng lifted the siege of Chong and went to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yao Xing attacked Hukong Fort; Deng lifted the siege of Chong and marched to meet him.

sentences.zh: 興因襲平涼。

translations.literal: Xing then raided Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Xing then raided Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 大獲而歸。

translations.literal: He took great booty and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He took great booty and returned.

sentences.zh: 萇使興還鎮長安。

translations.literal: Chang had Xing return to guard Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent Xing back to guard Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪以薛干太悉伏不送劉勃勃，八月，襲其城，屠之，太悉伏奔秦。

translations.literal: The Wei king Gui, because the Xuegan chief Taisifu would not hand over Liu Bobo, in the eighth month assaulted his city, slaughtered it, and Taisifu fled to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ruler Tuoba Gui, because the Xuegan chief Taisifu would not surrender Liu Bobo, assaulted his city in the eighth month, slaughtered it, and Taisifu fled to Qin.

sentences.zh: 氐帥楊佛嵩叛，奔後秦，楊佺期、趙睦追之，九月，丙戌，敗佛嵩於潼關。

translations.literal: The Di chieftain Yang Fosong rebelled and fled to Later Qin; Yang Quanqi and Zhao Mu pursued him, and in the ninth month, on bingxu, defeated Fosong at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Di chieftain Yang Fosong rebelled and fled to Later Qin; Yang Quanqi and Zhao Mu pursued him and, in the ninth month on bingxu, defeated him at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 後秦將姚崇救佛嵩，敗晉兵，趙睦死。

translations.literal: The Later Qin general Yao Chong rescued Fosong, defeated Jin troops, and Zhao Mu died.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin general Yao Chong rescued Fosong, defeated Jin troops, and Zhao Mu was killed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，後秦主萇疾甚，還長安。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Later Qin ruler Chang's illness grew grave and he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Yao Chang's illness grew grave and he returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂議伐西燕，諸將皆曰：「永未有釁，我連年征討，士卒疲弊，未可也。」

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Chui discussed attacking Western Yan. The generals all said: "Yong has given no provocation; we have campaigned year after year and the soldiers are weary and spent—it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui discussed attacking Western Yan. His generals said, "Yong has given no cause for war; we have campaigned year after year and the troops are exhausted—it cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 范陽王德曰：「永既國之枝葉，又僭舉位號，惑民視聽，宜行先除之，以壹民心。

translations.literal: Murong De, Prince of Fanyang, said: "Yong is both a branch of our state and has presumptuously taken titles and ranks, misleading the people's eyes and ears. We ought to move first to remove him and unify the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De of Fanyang said, "Yong is kin of our house yet has presumptuously taken royal titles and misled the people. We should remove him first and unify hearts.

sentences.zh: 士卒雖疲，庸得已乎！」

translations.literal: Though the soldiers are weary, how can we stop!"
translations.idiomatic: Though the troops are weary, how can we stop now!"

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「司徒意正與吾同。

translations.literal: Chui said: "The Minister over the Masses' intent is exactly the same as mine.
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "The Minister over the Masses thinks as I do.

sentences.zh: 吾比老，叩囊底智，足以取之，終不復留此賊以累子孫也。」

translations.literal: I am growing old; I shall tap the wisdom at the bottom of the bag—enough to take him. I will not leave this bandit to burden my descendants."
translations.idiomatic: I am old now, but the last of my wits is enough to take him. I will not leave this rogue to burden my descendants."

sentences.zh: 遂戒嚴。

translations.literal: He thereupon put the army on alert.
translations.idiomatic: He then mobilized the army.

sentences.zh: 十一月，垂發中山步騎七萬，遣鎮西將軍丹楊王纘，〔瓚〕、龍驤將軍張崇出井陘，攻西燕武鄉公友於晉陽，征東將軍平規攻鎮東將軍段平於沙亭。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Chui set out from Zhongshan with seventy thousand foot and horse, sent the General Who Guards the West Murong Zuan, Prince of Danyang, and the Dragon Cavalry General Zhang Chong out through Jingxing to attack You, Duke of Wuxiang of Western Yan, at Jinyang, and the General Who Conquers the East Ping Gui to attack Duan Ping, General Who Guards the East, at Shating.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Chui marched from Zhongshan with seventy thousand infantry and cavalry, sent General Who Guards the West Murong Zuan of Danyang and Dragon Cavalry General Zhang Chong through Jingxing against You, Duke of Wuxiang of Western Yan, at Jinyang, and General Who Conquers the East Ping Gui against Duan Ping at Shating.

sentences.zh: 西燕主永遣其尚書令刁雲、車騎將軍慕容鐘帥眾五萬守潞川。

translations.literal: The Western Yan ruler Yong sent his Director of the Masters of Writing Diao Yun and General of Chariots and Cavalry Murong Zhong to lead fifty thousand men to guard Luchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong sent his Director of the Masters of Writing Diao Yun and General of Chariots and Cavalry Murong Zhong with fifty thousand men to hold Luchuan.

sentences.zh: 友，永之弟也。

translations.literal: You was Yong's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: You was Yong's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 十二月，垂至鄴。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Chui reached Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Chui reached Ye.

sentences.zh: 己亥，後秦主萇召太尉姚旻、僕射尹緯、姚晃、將軍姚大目、尚書狄伯支入禁中，受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: On jihai the Later Qin ruler Chang summoned Grand Commandant Yao Min, Director of the Masters of Writing Yin Wei, Yao Huang, General Yao Damu, and Master of Writing Di Bozhi into the inner palace to receive the testamentary edict and assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Yao Chang summoned Grand Commandant Yao Min, Director Yin Wei, Yao Huang, General Yao Damu, and Master of Writing Di Bozhi into the inner palace to receive his deathbed edict and assist the government.

sentences.zh: 萇謂太子興曰：「有毀此諸公者，慎勿受之。

translations.literal: Chang said to the crown prince Xing: "If anyone slanders these lords, take care not to believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Chang told Crown Prince Xing, "If anyone slanders these men, do not believe it.

sentences.zh: 汝撫骨肉以恩，接大臣以禮，待物以信，遇民以仁，四者不失，吾無憂矣。」

translations.literal: Treat kinsmen with kindness, receive great ministers with ritual, handle affairs with trustworthiness, and meet the people with benevolence—if these four are not lost, I have no worries."
translations.idiomatic: Treat kin with kindness, ministers with courtesy, affairs with trustworthiness, and the people with benevolence—keep these four and I need not worry."

sentences.zh: 姚晃垂涕問取苻登之策，萇曰：「今大業垂成，興才智足辦，奚所復問！」

translations.literal: Yao Huang, weeping, asked the plan for taking Fu Deng. Chang said: "Now the great enterprise is nearly complete; Xing's talent and wisdom are sufficient to accomplish it—what is there left to ask!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Huang wept and asked how to defeat Fu Deng. Chang said, "The great enterprise is nearly done; Xing's talent is enough—what more is there to ask!"

sentences.zh: 庚子，萇卒。

translations.literal: On gengzi Chang died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Chang died.

sentences.zh: 興秘不發喪，以其叔父緒鎮安定，碩德鎮陰密，弟崇守長安。

translations.literal: Xing kept the death secret and did not announce mourning. He stationed his uncle Xu at Anding, Shuode at Yinmi, and his younger brother Chong to guard Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xing kept the death secret. He posted his uncle Xu at Anding, Shuode at Yinmi, and his brother Chong at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 或謂碩德曰：「公威名素重，部曲最強，今易世之際，必為朝廷所疑，不如且奔秦州，觀望事勢。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Shuode: "Your prestige has long been weighty and your private following the strongest. At this change of reign you are sure to be suspected by the court—better for now to flee to Qinzhou and watch how affairs develop."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Shuode, "Your prestige is great and your following the strongest. At a change of reign the court will surely suspect you—better flee to Qinzhou and watch events."

sentences.zh: 碩德曰：「太子志度寬明，必無它慮。

translations.literal: Shuode said: "The crown prince's aims and breadth are generous and clear; he is sure to have no other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Shuode said, "The crown prince is generous and clear-minded; he will harbor no other designs.

sentences.zh: 今苻登未滅而骨肉相攻，是自亡也。

translations.literal: Now Fu Deng is not yet destroyed, yet kinsmen attack one another—that is self-destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng is not yet destroyed, yet kin turn on kin—that is self-destruction.

sentences.zh: 吾有死而已，終不為也。」

translations.literal: I have only death—that is all—and in the end I will not do it."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die than do it."

sentences.zh: 遂往見興，興優禮而遣之。

translations.literal: He then went to see Xing; Xing treated him with exceptional courtesy and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: He went to see Xing, who received him with honor and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 興自稱是大將軍，以尹緯為長史，狄伯支為司馬，帥眾伐秦。

translations.literal: Xing styled himself Grand General, made Yin Wei Chief Clerk and Di Bozhi Marshal, and led the host to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Xing styled himself Grand General, made Yin Wei Chief Clerk and Di Bozhi Marshal, and marched against Qin.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝下太元十九年

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong, the nineteenth year of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong: the nineteenth year of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，秦主登聞後秦主萇卒，喜曰：「姚興小兒，吾折杖笞之耳。」

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Qin ruler Deng heard that the Later Qin ruler Chang had died and said in delight: "The boy Yao Xing—I can break a staff and flog him."
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Yao Deng heard that Yao Chang had died and rejoiced, "That boy Yao Xing—I can break a stick and beat him."

sentences.zh: 乃大赦，盡眾而東，留司徒安成王廣守雍，太子崇守胡空堡；

translations.literal: He then proclaimed a general amnesty, led out the entire host eastward, left the Minister over the Masses Murong Guang, Prince of Ancheng, to guard Yong, and the crown prince Chong to guard Hukong Fort;
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty, marched east with his whole army, left Minister over the Masses Murong Guang of Ancheng at Yong, and Crown Prince Chong at Hukong Fort;

sentences.zh: 遣使拜金城王乾歸為左丞相、河南王，領秦、梁、益、涼、沙五州牧，加九錫。

translations.literal: he sent envoys to invest Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng, as Left Chancellor and King of Henan, with charge as Governor of Qin, Liang, Yi, Liang, and Sha provinces, adding the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: and sent envoys to invest Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng, as Left Chancellor and King of Henan, Governor of five provinces, with the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 初，禿髮思復鞬卒，子烏孤立。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tufa Sifujian died and his son Wuji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Tufa Sifujian died and his son Wuji succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 烏孤雄勇有大志，與大將紛陀謀取涼州。

translations.literal: Wuji was bold, brave, and had great designs; with the great general Fentuo he plotted to take Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji was bold and ambitious; with his great general Fentuo he plotted to seize Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 紛陀曰：「公必欲得涼州，宜先務農講武，禮俊賢，修政刑，然後可也。」

translations.literal: Fentuo said: "If my lord must have Liangzhou, you should first devote yourself to agriculture and drill the troops, honor worthy men, and repair government and punishments—only then is it possible."
translations.idiomatic: Fentuo said, "If you mean to take Liangzhou, first promote farming and drill the troops, honor worthy men, and reform law and government—only then."

sentences.zh: 烏孤從之。

translations.literal: Wuji followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji agreed.

sentences.zh: 三河王光遣使拜烏孤冠軍大將軍、河西鮮卑大都統。

translations.literal: Lü Guang, King of Sanhe, sent envoys to invest Wuji as General-in-Chief of Champions and Grand Commander of the Hexi Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang sent envoys to invest Wuji as General-in-Chief of Champions and Grand Commander of the Hexi Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 烏孤與其群下謀之曰；

translations.literal: Wuji consulted his followers, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wuji consulted his followers:

sentences.zh: 「可受乎？」

translations.literal: "Can we accept this?"
translations.idiomatic: "Should we accept?"

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「吾士馬眾多，何為屬人？」

translations.literal: All said: "Our soldiers and horses are numerous—why submit to another?"
translations.idiomatic: All said, "Our warriors and horses are many—why submit to another?"

sentences.zh: 石真若留不對，烏孤曰：「卿畏呂光邪？」

translations.literal: Shi Zhenru did not answer. Wuji said: "Do you fear Lü Guang?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhenru was silent. Wuji said, "Do you fear Lü Guang?"

sentences.zh: 石真若留曰：「吾本根未固，小大非敵，若光致死於我，何以待之？

translations.literal: Shi Zhenru said: "Our roots are not yet firm; great and small are not matched. If Guang stakes his life against us, how shall we meet it?
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhenru said, "Our roots are not yet firm; we are no match for him. If Guang stakes everything against us, how shall we answer?

sentences.zh: 不如受，以驕之，俟釁而動，蔑不克矣。」

translations.literal: Better to accept and make him arrogant; wait for an opening and move—nothing will fail to be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Better accept and make him arrogant; wait for an opening and strike—then we cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 烏孤乃受之。

translations.literal: Wuji then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji accepted.

sentences.zh: 二月，秦主登攻屠各姚奴、帛蒲二堡，克之。

translations.literal: In the second month the Qin ruler Deng attacked the Tuge forts of Yao Nu and Bo Pu and took them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Yao Deng attacked the Tuge forts of Yao Nu and Bo Pu and took them.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂留清河公會鎮鄴，發司、冀、青、兗兵，遣太原王楷出滏口，遼西王農出壺關，垂自出沙庭，以擊西燕，標榜所趣，軍各就頓。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Chui left Murong Hui, Duke of Qinghe, to guard Ye, mobilized troops from Si, Ji, Qing, and Yan provinces, sent Murong Kai, Prince of Taiyuan, out through Fukou and Murong Nong, Prince of Liaoxi, out through Huguan; Chui himself went out from Shating to strike Western Yan. Proclaiming their destinations, each army went to its encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui left Murong Hui of Qinghe at Ye, mobilized troops from four provinces, sent Murong Kai of Taiyuan through Fukou and Murong Nong of Liaoxi through Huguan, and marched from Shating himself against Western Yan. Each column marched to its assigned camp.

sentences.zh: 西燕主永聞之，嚴兵分道拒守，聚糧台壁，遣從子征東將軍小逸豆歸、鎮東將軍王次多、右將軍勒馬駒帥眾萬餘人戍之。

translations.literal: When the Western Yan ruler Yong heard of this, he arrayed troops on separate routes to resist and defend, gathered grain at Taibi, and sent his nephew the General Who Conquers the East Xiao Yidougui, the General Who Guards the East Wang Ciduo, and the Right General Lemaju to lead more than ten thousand men to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong heard and drew up his forces on separate routes, stored grain at Taibi, and sent his nephew General Who Conquers the East Xiao Yidougui, General Who Guards the East Wang Ciduo, and Right General Lemaju with more than ten thousand men to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，秦主登自六陌趣廢橋，後秦始平太守姚詳據馬嵬堡以拒之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Qin ruler Deng went from Liumo toward Feiqiao; the Later Qin Administrator of Shiping Yao Xiang held Mawei Fort to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Yao Deng marched from Liumo toward Feiqiao; Later Qin Administrator of Shiping Yao Xiang held Mawei Fort against him.

sentences.zh: 太子興遣尹緯將兵救詳，緯據廢橋以待秦。

translations.literal: The crown prince Xing sent Yin Wei to lead troops to rescue Xiang; Wei held Feiqiao to await Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Xing sent Yin Wei to rescue Xiang; Wei held Feiqiao to await Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦兵爭水，不能得，渴死者什二、三，因急攻緯。

translations.literal: Qin troops struggled for water but could not obtain it; two or three tenths died of thirst, and they therefore pressed a fierce attack on Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Qin troops fought for water and could not get it; two or three in ten died of thirst, and they pressed a fierce attack on Wei.

sentences.zh: 興馳遣狄伯支謂緯曰：「苻登窮寇，宜持重以挫之。」

translations.literal: Xing urgently sent Di Bozhi to tell Wei: "Fu Deng is a cornered foe; you should hold steady and wear him down."
translations.idiomatic: Xing urgently sent Di Bozhi to tell Wei, "Fu Deng is cornered—hold steady and wear him down."

sentences.zh: 緯曰：「先帝登遐，人情擾懼，今不因思奮之力以禽敵，大事去矣！」

translations.literal: Wei said: "The late emperor has ascended afar; men's hearts are disturbed and fearful. If we do not now use the force of grief and resolve to capture the enemy, the great enterprise is lost!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "The late emperor is gone and hearts are unsettled. If we do not seize the enemy now with the force of grief and resolve, all is lost!"

sentences.zh: 遂與秦戰，秦兵大敗。

translations.literal: He then gave battle with Qin and Qin troops were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He gave battle and Qin was routed.

sentences.zh: 其夜，秦眾潰，登單騎奔雍。

translations.literal: That night the Qin host collapsed; Deng alone on horseback fled to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Qin army collapsed; Deng fled alone on horseback to Yong.

sentences.zh: 太子崇及安成王廣聞敗，皆棄城走；

translations.literal: The crown prince Chong and Murong Guang, Prince of Ancheng, hearing of the defeat, both abandoned their cities and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Chong and Murong Guang of Ancheng heard of the defeat and abandoned their cities;

sentences.zh: 登至，無所歸，乃奔平涼，收集遺眾，入馬毛山。

translations.literal: when Deng arrived there was nowhere to return; he then fled to Pingliang, gathered the scattered host, and entered Maomao Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: when Deng arrived he had nowhere to turn; he fled to Pingliang, gathered the remnants, and entered Maomao Mountain.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂頓軍鄴西南，月餘不進。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Chui halted his army southwest of Ye and for more than a month did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui halted southwest of Ye for more than a month without advancing.

sentences.zh: 西燕主永怪之，以為太行道寬，疑垂欲詭道取之，乃悉斂諸軍屯軹關，杜太行口，惟留台壁一軍。

translations.literal: The Western Yan ruler Yong thought it strange; believing the Taihang route wide, he suspected Chui meant to take him by a deceptive route. He therefore gathered all armies to encamp at Zhiguan, blocked the Taihang passes, and left only one army at Taibi.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong found it strange; thinking the Taihang route open, he suspected Chui meant to outflank him. He massed his armies at Zhiguan, blocked the Taihang passes, and left only one force at Taibi.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，垂引大軍出滏口，入天井關。

translations.literal: On jiaxu Chui led the great army out through Fukou and entered Tianjing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Chui led his main force through Fukou into Tianjing Pass.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙酉，燕軍至台壁，永遣從兄太尉大逸豆歸救之，平規擊破之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yiyou, Yan troops reached Taibi. Yong sent his elder cousin's son the Grand Commandant Da Yidougui to rescue it; Ping Gui defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yiyou, Yan reached Taibi. Yong sent his cousin Grand Commandant Da Yidougui to relieve it; Ping Gui defeated him.

sentences.zh: 小逸豆歸出戰，遼西王農又擊破之，斬勒馬駒，禽王次多，遂圍台壁。

translations.literal: Xiao Yidougui came out to fight; Murong Nong, Prince of Liaoxi, again defeated him, beheaded Lemaju, captured Wang Ciduo, and then besieged Taibi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yidougui sallied out; Murong Nong of Liaoxi defeated him again, beheaded Lemaju, captured Wang Ciduo, and besieged Taibi.

sentences.zh: 永召太行軍還，自將精兵五萬以拒之。

translations.literal: Yong recalled the Taihang armies and personally led fifty thousand picked troops to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong recalled his Taihang forces and led fifty thousand picked troops against him.

sentences.zh: 刁雲、慕容鐘震怖，帥眾降燕，永誅其妻子。

translations.literal: Diao Yun and Murong Zhong, shaken with terror, led their hosts to surrender to Yan; Yong executed their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yun and Murong Zhong, terrified, surrendered to Yan; Yong executed their families.

sentences.zh: 己亥，垂陳於台壁南，遣驍騎將軍慕容國伏千騎於澗下。

translations.literal: On jihai Chui drew up south of Taibi and sent the Valiant Cavalry General Murong Guo to lie in ambush with a thousand horse in the ravine below.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Chui formed battle lines south of Taibi and hid a thousand cavalry under Valiant Cavalry General Murong Guo in the ravine below.

sentences.zh: 庚子，與永合戰，垂偽退，永眾追之，行數里，國騎從澗中出，斷其後，諸軍四面俱進，大破之，斬首八千餘級，永走歸長子。

translations.literal: On gengzi he joined battle with Yong. Chui feigned retreat; Yong's host pursued him. After several li Guo's cavalry came out from the ravine and cut off their rear; all armies advanced from four sides and routed them utterly, taking more than eight thousand heads. Yong fled back to Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he fought Yong. Chui feigned retreat; Yong pursued. After several li Murong Guo's cavalry burst from the ravine and cut off their rear; Yan forces closed from all sides, killed more than eight thousand, and Yong fled to Changzi.

sentences.zh: 晉陽守將聞之，棄城走。

translations.literal: The defending general at Jinyang heard of this and abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinyang garrison heard and abandoned the city.

sentences.zh: 丹楊王瓚等進取晉陽。

translations.literal: Murong Zuan, Prince of Danyang, and others advanced to take Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zuan of Danyang and others advanced to take Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 後秦太子先始發喪，即皇帝位於槐里，大赦，改元皇初，遂如安定。

translations.literal: The Later Qin crown prince first announced mourning, then ascended the imperial throne at Huaili, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Huangchu, and then went to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Qin crown prince announced mourning, ascended the throne at Huaili, proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the era name Huangchu, and went to Anding.

sentences.zh: 謚後秦主萇曰武昭皇帝，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: He gave the posthumous title Martial and Illustrious Emperor to the Later Qin ruler Chang, with temple name Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Yao Chang the posthumous title Martial and Illustrious Emperor, with temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬子，追尊會稽王太妃鄭氏曰簡文宣太后。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renzi, Lady Zheng, consort of the Prince of Kuaiji, was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Jianwenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renzi, Lady Zheng, consort of the Prince of Kuaiji, was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Jianwenxuan.

sentences.zh: 群臣謂宣太后應配食元帝，太子前率徐邈曰：「宣太后平素之時，不伉儷於先帝。

translations.literal: The ministers said the Empress Dowager Xuan should share sacrifices with Emperor Yuan. Xu Miao, Leader of the Heir Apparent's Front Guard, said: "In her ordinary life the Empress Dowager Xuan was not a proper consort to the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers said Empress Dowager Xuan should share sacrifices with Emperor Yuan. Xu Miao, Leader of the Heir Apparent's Front Guard, said, "In life Empress Dowager Xuan was not a proper consort to the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 至於子孫，豈可為祖考立配！」

translations.literal: As for descendants, how can we set her as consort to an ancestral grandfather!"
translations.idiomatic: As for descendants, how can we pair her with an ancestral grandfather!"

sentences.zh: 國學明教東莞臧燾曰：「今尊號既正，則罔極之情申；

translations.literal: Zang Tao of Dongguan, Instructor of the National University, said: "Now that the honored title is correct, boundless filial feeling is expressed;
translations.idiomatic: Zang Tao of Dongguan, Instructor of the National University, said, "Now that her honored title is settled, boundless filial feeling is expressed;

sentences.zh: 別建寢廟，則嚴檷之義顯；

translations.literal: if a separate temple is built, the meaning of strict father and humble mother is made clear;
translations.idiomatic: if a separate temple is built, the principle of honoring father and mother in their proper stations is clear;

sentences.zh: 系子為稱，兼明貴之所由。

translations.literal: to take the son as the title also shows whence dignity arises.
translations.idiomatic: to take the son as the title also shows the source of her dignity.

sentences.zh: 一舉而允三義，不亦善乎？」

translations.literal: One act satisfying three principles—is it not good?"
translations.idiomatic: One act satisfying three principles—is that not best?"

sentences.zh: 乃立廟於太廟路西。

translations.literal: A temple was then established west of the Imperial Ancestral Temple road.
translations.idiomatic: A temple was established west of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂進軍圍長子。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Chui advanced and besieged Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui advanced and besieged Changzi.

sentences.zh: 西燕主永欲奔後秦，侍中蘭英曰：「昔石虎伐龍都，太祖堅守不去，卒成大燕之基。

translations.literal: The Western Yan ruler Yong wished to flee to Later Qin. Lan Ying, Palace Attendant, said: "In the past when Shi Hu attacked Longdu, the Founding Ancestor held firm and did not leave, and in the end the foundation of Great Yan was secured.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong wished to flee to Later Qin. Lan Ying, Palace Attendant, said, "When Shi Hu attacked Longdu, our founding ancestor held firm and in the end secured Great Yan's foundation.

sentences.zh: 今垂七十老翁，厭苦兵革，終不能頓兵連歲以攻我也。

translations.literal: Now Chui is a seventy-year-old man, weary and bitter at arms—he cannot in the end halt his troops year after year to attack us.
translations.idiomatic: Chui is a seventy-year-old man, weary of war—he cannot camp here year after year against us.

sentences.zh: 但當城守以疲之。」

translations.literal: We need only hold the city and wear him down."
translations.idiomatic: We need only hold the walls and wear him down."

sentences.zh: 永從之。

translations.literal: Yong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Yong agreed.

sentences.zh: 秦主登遣其子汝陰王宗為質於河南王乾歸以請救，進封乾歸梁王，納其妹為梁王后。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng sent his son Zong, Prince of Ruyin, as hostage to Qifu Gangui, King of Henan, to seek rescue; he advanced Gangui to King of Liang and took his younger sister as Queen of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Deng sent his son Zong, Prince of Ruyin, as hostage to Qifu Gangui, King of Henan, to seek aid; he created Gangui King of Liang and took Gangui's sister as queen.

sentences.zh: 乾歸遣前軍將軍乞伏益州等帥騎一萬救之。

translations.literal: Gangui sent the Forward Army General Qifu Yizhou and others to lead ten thousand horse to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui sent Forward Army General Qifu Yizhou and others with ten thousand cavalry to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，登引兵出迎乾歸兵。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Deng led troops out to meet Gangui's forces.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Deng marched out to meet Gangui's forces.

sentences.zh: 後秦主興自安定如涇陽，與登戰於山南，執登，殺之。

translations.literal: The Later Qin ruler Xing went from Anding to Jingyang, fought Deng south of the mountain, captured him, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin ruler Yao Xing marched from Anding to Jingyang, fought Deng south of the mountain, captured him, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 悉散其部眾，使歸農業，徙陰密三萬戶於長安，以李後賜姚晃。

translations.literal: He fully dispersed Deng's forces, sent them back to farming, moved thirty thousand households from Yinmi to Chang'an, and gave Empress Li to Yao Huang.
translations.idiomatic: He fully dispersed Deng's troops, sent them back to farming, moved thirty thousand households from Yinmi to Chang'an, and gave Empress Li to Yao Huang.

sentences.zh: 益州等聞之，引兵還。

translations.literal: Yizhou and the others, hearing this, led their troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Yizhou and the others, hearing this, withdrew their troops.

sentences.zh: 秦太子崇奔湟中，即帝位，改元延初。

translations.literal: The Qin crown prince Chong fled to Huangzhong, thereupon took the imperial throne, and changed the era name to Yanchu.
translations.idiomatic: Qin crown prince Yao Chong fled to Huangzhong, took the throne, and changed the era name to Yanchu.

sentences.zh: 謚登曰高皇帝，廟號太宗。

translations.literal: He gave Deng the posthumous title Emperor Gao and the temple name Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously titled Deng Emperor Gao and gave him the temple name Taizong.

sentences.zh: 後秦安南將軍強熙、鎮遠將軍楊多叛，推竇沖為主。

translations.literal: Later Qin General Who Pacifies the South Qiang Xi and General Who Pacifies the Distant Yang Duo rebelled and set Dou Chong up as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin Generals Qiang Xi and Yang Duo rebelled and made Dou Chong their leader.

sentences.zh: 後秦主興自將討之，軍至武功，多兄子良國殺多而降，熙奔秦州，衝奔汧川，汧川氐仇高執送之。

translations.literal: Later Qin ruler Xing personally led troops to suppress them. When the army reached Wugong, Yang Duo's elder brother's son Liangguo killed Duo and surrendered. Xi fled to Qinzhou; Chong fled to Qianchuan, where the Di leader Qiu Gao of Qianchuan seized and delivered him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin ruler Yao Xing marched in person to suppress them. At Wugong, Yang Duo's nephew Liangguo killed Duo and surrendered. Xi fled to Qinzhou; Chong fled to Qianchuan, where the Di leader Qiu Gao seized and handed him over.

sentences.zh: 三河王光以子覆為都督玉門以西諸軍事、西域大都護，鎮高昌，命大臣子弟隨之。

translations.literal: King of Three Rivers Lü Guang appointed his son Fu Governor of All Military Affairs west of Yumen and Grand Protector of the Western Regions, stationed at Gaochang, and ordered the sons of his chief ministers to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: King of Three Rivers Lü Guang made his son Fu commander of all forces west of Yumen and Grand Protector of the Western Regions, stationed him at Gaochang, and ordered the sons of his chief ministers to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 八月，己巳，尊皇太妃李氏為皇太后，居崇訓宮。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jisi, the Imperial Noble Consort Lady Li was honored as Empress Dowager and resided in the Chongxun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jisi, Imperial Noble Consort Lady Li was honored as empress dowager and took up residence in Chongxun Palace.

sentences.zh: 西燕主永困急，遣其子常山公弘等求救於雍州刺史郗恢，並獻玉璽一紐。

translations.literal: Western Yan ruler Yong, pressed hard, sent his son Hong, Duke of Changshan, and others to beg rescue from Xi Hui, Inspector of Yong Province, and also presented one imperial seal cord.
translations.idiomatic: Western Yan ruler Murong Yong, hard pressed, sent his son Hong, Duke of Changshan, and others to beg aid from Xi Hui, Inspector of Yong Province, and also presented an imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 恢上言：「垂若並永，為患益深，不如兩存之，可以乘機雙斃。」

translations.literal: Hui memorialized the throne: "If Chui annexes Yong, the harm will grow deeper; it would be better to keep both alive, so we may seize the moment and destroy them both."
translations.idiomatic: Hui memorialized the throne: "If Chui swallows Yong, the danger will only deepen. Better to let both survive so we can seize the moment and destroy them both."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，詔青、兗二州刺史王恭、豫州刺史庾楷救之。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought this right and ordered Wang Gong, Inspector of Qing and Yan provinces, and Yu Kai, Inspector of Yu Province, to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered Wang Gong, Inspector of Qing and Yan, and Yu Kai, Inspector of Yu, to go to his aid.

sentences.zh: 楷，亮之孫也。

translations.literal: Kai was the grandson of Yu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was Yu Liang's grandson.

sentences.zh: 永恐晉兵不出，又遣其太子亮為質；

translations.literal: Yong, fearing that Jin troops would not come out, also sent his crown prince Liang as hostage;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Jin troops would not march out, Yong also sent Crown Prince Liang as hostage;

sentences.zh: 平規追亮，及於高都，獲之。

translations.literal: Ping Gui pursued Liang, caught up with him at Gaodu, and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Gui pursued Liang, caught up with him at Gaodu, and captured him.

sentences.zh: 永又告急於魏，魏王珪遣陳留公虔、將軍庾岳帥騎五萬東渡河，屯秀容，以救之。

translations.literal: Yong also sent urgent word to Wei. Wei King Tuoba Gui sent Chenliu Duke Que and General Yu Yue to lead fifty thousand horse east across the Yellow River, encamp at Xiurong, and rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong also appealed to Wei. Wei King Tuoba Gui sent Chenliu Duke Que and General Yu Yue with fifty thousand cavalry east across the Yellow River to encamp at Xiurong and rescue him.

sentences.zh: 虔，紇根之子也。

translations.literal: Que was the son of Hela Gen.
translations.idiomatic: Que was the son of Hela Gen.

sentences.zh: 晉、魏兵皆未至，大逸豆歸部將伐勤等開門內燕兵，燕人執永，斬之，並斬其公卿大將刁雲、大逸豆歸等三十餘人，得永所統八郡七萬餘戶及秦乘輿、服御、伎樂、珍寶甚眾。

translations.literal: Neither Jin nor Wei troops had yet arrived when Dayidougui's subordinate general Faqin and others opened the gates and admitted Yan troops. The Yan men seized Yong and beheaded him, also beheading more than thirty of his ministers, generals, and great officers including Diao Yun and Dayidougui. They obtained the eight commanderies and more than seventy thousand households under Yong's rule, together with very many of Qin's imperial carriages, regalia, performers, and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Before Jin or Wei troops arrived, Dayidougui's officer Faqin and others opened the gates to Yan forces. The Yan seized Yong and executed him, along with more than thirty of his ministers and generals, including Diao Yun and Dayidougui. They took the eight commanderies and more than seventy thousand households under Yong's rule, as well as Qin's imperial carriages, regalia, performers, and a great store of treasures.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂以丹楊王瓚為并州刺史，鎮晉陽；

translations.literal: Yan ruler Chui appointed Dan'yang Wang Zan Inspector of Bing Province and stationed him at Jinyang;
translations.idiomatic: Yan ruler Murong Chui made Dan'yang Wang Zan Inspector of Bing Province and stationed him at Jinyang;

sentences.zh: 宜都王鳳為雍州刺史，鎮長子。

translations.literal: Yidu Wang Feng Inspector of Yong Province and stationed him at Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: and Yidu Wang Feng Inspector of Yong Province, stationed at Changzi.

sentences.zh: 永尚書僕射昌黎屈遵、尚書陽平王德、秘書監中山李先、太子詹事渤海封則、黃門郎太山胡母亮、中書郎張騰、尚書郎燕郡公孫表皆隨才擢敘。

translations.literal: Yong's Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Qu Zun of Changli, Master of Writing Murong De, Prince of Yangping, Director of the Secretariat Li Xian of Zhongshan, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent Feng Ze of Bohai, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Humu Liang of Taishan, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat Zhang Teng, and Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Gongsun Biao of Yanzhi were all promoted and assigned according to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's former officials—Vice Director Qu Zun of Changli, Master of Writing Murong De of Yangping, Secretariat Director Li Xian of Zhongshan, Heir Apparent Tutor Feng Ze of Bohai, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Humu Liang of Taishan, Palace Secretariat Gentleman Zhang Teng, and Masters of Writing Gentleman Gongsun Biao of Yanzhi—were all promoted according to their abilities.

sentences.zh: 九月，垂自長子如鄴。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Chui went from Changzi to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Chui went from Changzi to Ye.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，秦主崇為梁王乾歸所逐，奔隴西王楊定。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Qin ruler Chong was driven off by Liang King Gangui and fled to Longxi King Yang Ding.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Qin ruler Yao Chong was driven off by Liang King Qifu Gangui and fled to Longxi King Yang Ding.

sentences.zh: 定留司馬邵強守秦州，帥眾二萬與崇共攻乾歸，乾歸遣涼州牧軻彈、秦州牧益州、立義將軍詰歸帥騎三萬拒之。

translations.literal: Ding left Sima Shao Qiang to hold Qinzhou, led twenty thousand men with Chong to attack Gangui, and Gangui sent Liangzhou Governor Kepan, Qinzhou Governor Yizhou, and General Who Establishes Righteousness Jigui to lead thirty thousand horse to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Ding left Sima Shao Qiang to hold Qinzhou and led twenty thousand men with Chong to attack Gangui. Gangui sent Liangzhou Governor Kepan, Qinzhou Governor Qifu Yizhou, and General Who Establishes Righteousness Jigui with thirty thousand cavalry to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 益州與定戰，敗於平州。

translations.literal: Yizhou fought Ding and was defeated at Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou fought Ding and was defeated at Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 軻彈、詰歸皆引退，軻彈司馬翟□奮劍怒曰：「主上以雄武開基，所向無敵，威振秦、蜀。

translations.literal: Kepan and Jigui both led their forces in withdrawal. Kepan's Chief Clerk Zhai Wei drew his sword angrily and said: "Our lord, with heroic martial bearing, founded the enterprise; wherever he turned none could stand against him, and his prestige shook Qin and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Kepan and Jigui both withdrew. Kepan's chief clerk Zhai Wei drew his sword and said angrily, "Our lord founded his realm with heroic martial prowess; none could stand before him, and his prestige shook Qin and Shu.

sentences.zh: 將軍以宗室居元帥之任，當竭力致命以佐國家。

translations.literal: You, General, as a member of the imperial clan hold the commander's post—you ought to exert your strength unto death to assist the state.
translations.idiomatic: You are of the imperial clan and hold command—you should spend yourself unto death for the state.

sentences.zh: 今秦州雖敗，二軍尚全，奈何望風退衄，將何面以見主上乎？

translations.literal: Though Qinzhou has now been defeated, the two armies are still intact—how can you flee at the first sign of trouble? With what face will you see our lord?
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou has fallen, yet two armies remain intact—why flee at the first setback? What face will you show our lord?

sentences.zh: □雖無任，獨不能以便宜斬將軍乎？」

translations.literal: Though Zhai Wei lacks official rank, cannot he on his own authority execute the general?"
translations.idiomatic: I may lack rank, but cannot I execute you on my own authority?"

sentences.zh: 軻彈謝曰：「向者未知眾心何如耳。

translations.literal: Kepan apologized and said: "Earlier I did not know how the troops' hearts stood.
translations.idiomatic: Kepan apologized: "I did not know before how the men felt.

sentences.zh: 果能如是，吾敢愛死？」

translations.literal: If you truly mean that, how dare I spare my own life?"
translations.idiomatic: If you truly mean that, how dare I spare my life?"

sentences.zh: 乃帥騎進戰，益州、詰歸亦勒兵繼之，大敗定兵，殺定及崇，斬首萬七千級。

translations.literal: He then led his horsemen forward to battle; Yizhou and Jigui also drove their troops after him, routed Ding's army utterly, killed Ding and Chong, and took seventeen thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his cavalry forward. Yizhou and Jigui rallied their troops and followed, crushing Ding's army, killing Ding and Chong, and taking seventeen thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 乾歸於是盡有隴西之地。

translations.literal: Gangui thereby came to possess all the lands of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui thereby came to hold all of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 定無子，其叔父佛狗之子盛，先守仇池，自稱征西將軍、秦州刺史、仇池公，謚定為武王，仍遣使來稱籓。

translations.literal: Ding had no son. His uncle Fogou's son Sheng, who had earlier held Qiuchi, styled himself General Who Conquers the West, Inspector of Qin Province, and Duke of Qiuchi, gave Ding the posthumous title King Wu, and still sent envoys to declare himself a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Ding had no son. His uncle Fogou's son Sheng, who had been holding Qiuchi, styled himself General Who Conquers the West, Inspector of Qin Province, and Duke of Qiuchi, posthumously titled Ding King Wu, and sent envoys to declare vassalage.

sentences.zh: 秦太子宣奔盛，盛分氐、羌為二十部護軍，各為鎮戍，不置郡縣。

translations.literal: The Qin crown prince Xuan fled to Sheng. Sheng divided the Di and Qiang into twenty Protectorates of the Army, each garrisoned in its own post, and did not establish commanderies or counties.
translations.idiomatic: Qin crown prince Xuan fled to Sheng. Sheng divided the Di and Qiang into twenty army protectorates, each with its own garrison, and set up no commanderies or counties.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂東巡陽平、平原，命遼西王農濟河，與安南將軍尹國略地青、兗。

translations.literal: Yan ruler Chui toured east through Yangping and Pingyuan, ordered Liaoxi Wang Nong to cross the river, and together with General Who Pacifies the South Yin Guo to seize territory in Qing and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ruler Chui toured east through Yangping and Pingyuan, ordered Liaoxi Wang Murong Nong to cross the river, and with General Who Pacifies the South Yin Guo to seize land in Qing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 農攻廩丘，國攻陽城，皆拔之。

translations.literal: Nong attacked Linqiu and Guo attacked Yangcheng; both were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Nong took Linqiu and Guo took Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 東平太守韋簡戰死，高平、太山、琅邪諸郡皆委城奔潰，農進軍臨海，遍置守宰。

translations.literal: Dongping Administrator Wei Jian died in battle. The commanderies of Gaoping, Taishan, and Langya all abandoned their cities and fled in rout. Nong advanced to the seacoast and set up governors and magistrates everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Dongping Administrator Wei Jian fell in battle. Gaoping, Taishan, Langya, and other commanderies abandoned their cities and fled. Nong marched to the coast and installed officials throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 柔然曷多汗棄其父，與社侖帥眾西走；

translations.literal: The Rouran chief Yedouhan abandoned his father and led his forces west in flight with Shelun;
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran chief Yedouhan abandoned his father and fled west with Shelun;

sentences.zh: 魏長孫肥追之，及於上郡跋那山，斬曷多汗。

translations.literal: Wei commander Zhangsun Fei pursued them, caught up at Banashan in Shang Commandery, and beheaded Yedouhan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei commander Zhangsun Fei pursued them, caught up at Banashan in Shang Commandery, and killed Yedouhan.

sentences.zh: 社侖收其餘眾數百，奔疋候跋，疋候跋處之南鄙。

translations.literal: Shelun gathered the several hundred survivors and fled to Pihou Ba; Pihou Ba settled them on his southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun gathered several hundred survivors and fled to Pihou Ba, who settled them on his southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 社侖襲疋候跋，殺之；

translations.literal: Shelun attacked Pihou Ba and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: Shelun attacked Pihou Ba and killed him;

sentences.zh: 疋候跋子啟跋、吳頡等皆奔魏。

translations.literal: Pihou Ba's sons Qiba, Wu Ti, and others all fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Pihou Ba's sons Qiba, Wu Ti, and others all fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 社侖掠五原以西諸部，走度漠北。

translations.literal: Shelun plundered the tribes west of Wuyuan and fled north across the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun raided the tribes west of Wuyuan and fled north across the desert.

sentences.zh: 十一月，燕遼西王農敗辟閭渾於龍水，遂入臨淄。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yan's Liaoxi Wang Nong defeated Pilü Hun on the Long River and then entered Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Yan's Liaoxi Wang Nong defeated Pilü Hun on the Long River and entered Linzi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，燕主垂召農等還。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Yan ruler Chui recalled Nong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Yan ruler Chui recalled Nong and the others.

sentences.zh: 秦主興遣使與燕結好，並送太子寶之子敏於燕，燕封敏為河東公。

translations.literal: Qin ruler Xing sent envoys to conclude friendly relations with Yan and also sent Crown Prince Bao's son Min to Yan; Yan enfeoffed Min as Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Qin ruler Yao Xing sent envoys to make peace with Yan and sent Crown Prince Murong Bao's son Min to Yan; Yan created Min Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 梁王乾歸自稱秦王，大赦。

translations.literal: Liang King Gangui styled himself King of Qin and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Liang King Qifu Gangui styled himself King of Qin and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝下太元二十年

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong, the twentieth year of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong: the twentieth year of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，燕主垂遣散騎常侍封則報聘於秦；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Yan ruler Chui sent Regular Palace Attendant Feng Ze on a return mission of courtesy to Qin;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Yan ruler Chui sent Regular Palace Attendant Feng Ze on a return mission to Qin;

sentences.zh: 遂自平原狩於廣川、勃海、長樂而歸。

translations.literal: he then hunted from Pingyuan through Guangchuan, Bohai, and Changle and returned.
translations.idiomatic: then hunted from Pingyuan through Guangchuan, Bohai, and Changle and returned.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸以太子熾磐領尚書令，左長史邊芮為左僕射，右長史秘宜為右僕射，置官皆如魏武、晉文故事，然猶稱大單于、大將軍。

translations.literal: Western Qin King Gangui had Crown Prince Chipan head the Masters of Writing, Left Chief Clerk Bian Rui serve as Left Vice Director, and Right Chief Clerk Mi Yi serve as Right Vice Director; all offices were established according to the precedents of Wei Wu and Jin Wen, yet he still styled himself Grand Chanyu and Grand General.
