translations.idiomatic: Western Qin King Gangui made Crown Prince Qifu Chipan head of the Masters of Writing, Left Chief Clerk Bian Rui Left Vice Director, and Right Chief Clerk Mi Yi Right Vice Director, establishing offices on the model of Cao Wu and Jin Wen, yet still styled himself Grand Chanyu and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 邊芮等領府佐如故。

translations.literal: Bian Rui and the others continued to head the staff of the headquarters as before.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Rui and the others continued to head the headquarters staff as before.

sentences.zh: 薛干太悉伏自長安亡歸嶺北，上郡以西鮮卑雜胡皆應之。

translations.literal: The Xuegan chief Taixifu fled from Chang'an and returned to the country north of the ridges; the Xianbei and mixed tribes west of Shang Commandery all responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuegan chief Taixifu fled Chang'an for the country north of the ridges, and Xianbei and mixed tribes west of Shang Commandery all rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲寅，尚書令陸納卒。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiayin, Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Na died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiayin, Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Na died.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚辰朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day of the month, gengchen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day gengchen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 皇太子出就東宮，以丹楊尹王雅領少傅。

translations.literal: The crown prince moved out to the Eastern Palace, and Dan'yang Prefect Wang Ya was appointed Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince moved to the Eastern Palace, and Dan'yang Prefect Wang Ya was made Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 時會稽王道子專權奢縱，嬖人趙牙本出倡優，茹千秋本錢唐捕賊吏，皆以諂賂得進。

translations.literal: At this time Prince of Kuaiji Daozi monopolized power and lived in luxury and excess. His favorite Zhao Ya had originally come from among entertainers, and Ru Qianqiu had originally been a thief-catching clerk in Qiantang; both advanced through flattery and bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi held sole power and lived in luxury. His favorite Zhao Ya had been an entertainer, and Ru Qianqiu a thief-catching clerk in Qiantang; both had risen through flattery and bribery.

sentences.zh: 道子以牙為魏郡太守，千秋為驃騎咨議參軍。

translations.literal: Daozi made Ya Administrator of Wei Commandery and Qianqiu Consulting Aide of the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi made Ya Administrator of Wei Commandery and Qianqiu Consulting Aide to the Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 牙為道子開東第，築山穿池，功用巨萬。

translations.literal: Ya opened an Eastern Residence for Daozi, building hills and digging ponds at a cost of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Ya built Daozi an Eastern Residence, piling hills and digging ponds at enormous expense.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗幸其第，謂道子曰：「府內乃有山，甚善；

translations.literal: The Emperor once visited the residence and said to Daozi: "To have a mountain within the mansion is very fine;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once visited the residence and said to Daozi, "A mountain inside the mansion is splendid;

sentences.zh: 然修飾太過。」

translations.literal: yet the ornamentation is excessive."
translations.idiomatic: but the ornamentation is excessive."

sentences.zh: 道子無以對。

translations.literal: Daozi had nothing to say in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi had no reply.

sentences.zh: 帝去，道子謂牙曰：「上若知山是人力所為，爾必死矣！」

translations.literal: After the Emperor left, Daozi said to Ya: "If His Majesty learns the mountain was made by human labor, you will surely die!"
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor left, Daozi said to Ya, "If His Majesty learns the mountain was made by hand, you will surely die!"

sentences.zh: 牙曰：「公在，牙何敢死！」

translations.literal: Ya said: "While you are here, how dare Ya die!"
translations.idiomatic: Ya said, "While you live, how dare I die!"

sentences.zh: 營作彌甚。

translations.literal: Construction grew ever more elaborate.
translations.idiomatic: Construction grew ever more lavish.

sentences.zh: 千秋賣官招權，聚貨累億。

translations.literal: Qianqiu sold offices to gather power and amassed wealth reaching hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqiu sold offices for power and amassed wealth in the hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 博平令吳興聞人奭上疏言之，帝益惡道子，而逼於太后，不忍廢黜，乃擢時望及所親幸王恭、卻恢、殷仲堪、王珣、王雅等，使居內外要任以防道子。

translations.literal: Wuxing Commandery's Boping Magistrate Wenren Shi memorialized about this. The Emperor came to hate Daozi all the more, but pressed by the Empress Dowager could not bear to depose him. He therefore promoted men of the day's reputation and those he personally favored—Wang Gong, Que Hui, Yin Zhongkan, Wang Xun, Wang Ya, and others—and placed them in key posts inside and outside the court to guard against Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: Boping Magistrate Wenren Shi of Wuxing memorialized about this. The emperor hated Daozi all the more, but bound by the empress dowager could not bear to remove him. He therefore promoted men of standing and personal favorites—Wang Gong, Que Hui, Yin Zhongkan, Wang Xun, and Wang Ya—and placed them in key posts at court and in the provinces to check Daozi.

sentences.zh: 道子亦引王國及國寶從弟琅邪內史緒，以為心腹。

translations.literal: Daozi also brought in Wang Guo and Guo's younger cousin from his mother's side Xu, Interior Secretary of Langya, as his trusted confidants.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi also brought in Wang Guo and Guo's maternal cousin Xu, Interior Secretary of Langya, as his trusted men.

sentences.zh: 由是朋黨競起，無復向時友愛之歡矣；

translations.literal: From this partisan factions sprang up in rivalry, and there was no longer the former affection among friends;
translations.idiomatic: Partisan factions then sprang up, and the old bonds of friendship were gone;

sentences.zh: 太后每和解之。

translations.literal: the Empress Dowager repeatedly mediated to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: the empress dowager repeatedly tried to reconcile them.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎徐邈從容言於帝曰：「漢文明主，猶悔淮南；

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Vice Director Xu Miao spoke calmly to the Emperor: "Emperor Wen of Han, though an enlightened ruler, still regretted Huainan;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Vice Director Xu Miao spoke calmly to the emperor: "Emperor Wen of Han, though enlightened, still regretted Huainan;

sentences.zh: 世祖聰達，負愧齊王。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, though perspicacious, bore guilt toward the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, though perspicacious, bore guilt toward the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 兄弟之際，實為深慎。

translations.literal: In matters between brothers, one must in truth be deeply cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Between brothers, one must be deeply cautious.

sentences.zh: 會稽王雖有酣媟之累，宜加弘貸，消散群議，外為國家之計，內慰太后之心。」

translations.literal: Though the Prince of Kuaiji has the fault of drunken excess, he ought to be treated with broad forbearance, public talk dispersed, outwardly for the state's sake and inwardly to comfort the Empress Dowager's heart."
translations.idiomatic: Though the Prince of Kuaiji has faults of drunken excess, he should be treated with broad forbearance, public talk quieted, outwardly for the state's sake and inwardly to comfort the empress dowager."

sentences.zh: 帝納之，復委任道子如故。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted this and restored Daozi to his former trust and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this and restored Daozi to his former trust.

sentences.zh: 初，楊定之死也，天水姜乳襲據上邽；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yang Ding died, Jiang Ru of Tianshui seized and held Shanggui;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yang Ding died, Jiang Ru of Tianshui seized Shanggui;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，西秦王乾歸遣乞伏益州帥騎六千討之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Western Qin King Gangui sent Qifu Yizhou to lead six thousand horse to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Western Qin King Gangui sent Qifu Yizhou with six thousand cavalry to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 左僕射邊芮、民部尚書王松壽曰：「益州屢勝而驕，不可專任。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Bian Rui and Minister of the People Wang Songshou said: "Yizhou, having won repeatedly, has grown arrogant and cannot be entrusted alone.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Bian Rui and Minister of the People Wang Songshou said, "Yizhou has grown arrogant after repeated victories and cannot be left in sole command.

sentences.zh: 必以輕敵取敗。」

translations.literal: He is sure to meet defeat through underestimating the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: He is sure to fall through underestimating the enemy."

sentences.zh: 乾歸曰：「益州驍勇，諸將莫及，當以重佐輔之耳。」

translations.literal: Gangui said: "Yizhou is fierce and brave; none of the generals can match him—he should simply be given weighty assistants to support him."
translations.idiomatic: Gangui said, "Yizhou is the bravest of our generals—he needs only weighty assistants to support him."

sentences.zh: 乃以平北將軍韋虔為長史，左禁將軍務和為司馬。

translations.literal: He then made General Who Pacifies the North Wei Qian Chief Clerk and Left Prohibitions General Wu He Army Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He then made General Who Pacifies the North Wei Qian chief clerk and Left Prohibitions General Wu He army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 至大寒嶺，益州不設部伍，聽將士游畋縱飲，令曰：「敢言軍事者斬！」

translations.literal: When they reached Dahan Ridge, Yizhou did not set up battle formations, allowed officers and soldiers to hunt and drink freely, and ordered: "Whoever dares speak of military matters shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: At Dahan Ridge, Yizhou formed no battle lines, let his men hunt and drink freely, and ordered, "Whoever speaks of military matters shall be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 虔等諫不聽，乳逆擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Qian and the others remonstrated but were not heeded; Ru struck back and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Qian and the others remonstrated in vain; Ru counterattacked and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪叛燕，侵逼附塞諸部。

translations.literal: Wei King Tuoba Gui rebelled against Yan and pressed and threatened the tribes attached to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Wei King Tuoba Gui rebelled against Yan and pressed the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲戌，燕主垂遣太子寶、遼西王農、趙王麟帥眾八萬，自五原伐魏，范陽王德、陳留王紹別將步騎萬八千為後繼。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiaxu, Yan ruler Chui sent Crown Prince Bao, Liaoxi Wang Nong, and Zhao Wang Lin to lead eighty thousand men from Wuyuan to attack Wei; Fanyang Wang De and Chenliu Wang Shao separately commanded eighteen thousand foot and horse as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiaxu, Yan ruler Chui sent Crown Prince Murong Bao, Liaoxi Wang Nong, and Zhao Wang Murong Lin with eighty thousand men from Wuyuan against Wei; Fanyang Wang Murong De and Chenliu Wang Murong Shao followed with eighteen thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍高湖諫曰：「魏與燕世為昏姻，彼有內難，燕實存之，其施德厚矣，結好久矣。

translations.literal: Regular Palace Attendant Gao Hu remonstrated: "Wei and Yan have been marriage kin for generations. When they had internal troubles, Yan in truth preserved them; the grace shown was deep, and the bond of friendship long.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Palace Attendant Gao Hu remonstrated: "Wei and Yan have been marriage kin for generations. When Wei had internal troubles, Yan preserved them—the grace was deep and the bond long.

sentences.zh: 間以求馬不獲而留其弟，曲在於我，奈何遽興兵擊之！

translations.literal: Recently, when we sought horses and did not recover them and detained his younger brother, the wrong was on our side—how can we suddenly raise troops and attack them!
translations.idiomatic: Recently we sought horses in vain and detained his brother—the fault was ours. How can we suddenly march against them!

sentences.zh: 拓跋涉珪沉勇有謀，幼歷艱難，兵精馬強，未易輕也。

translations.literal: Tuoba Shegui is deep, brave, and scheming; from youth he has passed through hardship; his soldiers are elite and his horses strong—not easily to be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Shegui is deep, brave, and scheming; he has known hardship since youth; his troops are elite and his horses strong—not to be taken lightly.

sentences.zh: 皇太子富於春秋，志果氣銳，今委之專征，必小魏而易之，萬一不如所欲，傷威毀重，願陛下深圖之！」

translations.literal: The crown prince is still young in years, resolute in will and sharp in spirit; now entrusted with sole command of the campaign, he is sure to make light of Wei and treat it easily. If by any chance things do not go as wished, prestige will be wounded and weight destroyed—I beg Your Majesty to think deeply on this!"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is young, resolute, and eager; given sole command, he is sure to underestimate Wei. If things go wrong, prestige will be lost—I beg Your Majesty to think deeply on this!"

sentences.zh: 言頗激切。

translations.literal: His words were rather sharp and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: His words were sharp and urgent.

sentences.zh: 垂怒，免湖官。

translations.literal: Chui was angry and dismissed Hu from office.
translations.idiomatic: Chui was angry and dismissed Hu from office.

sentences.zh: 湖，泰之子也。

translations.literal: Hu was the son of Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was the son of Tai.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸丑，燕太原元王楷卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guichou, Yan's Taiyuan Yuan Wang Kai died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guichou, Yan's Taiyuan Yuan Wang Murong Kai died.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸遷於西城。

translations.literal: Western Qin King Gangui moved his capital to Xicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Western Qin King Gangui moved his capital to Xicheng.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，三河王光帥眾十萬伐西秦，西秦左輔密貴周、左衛將軍莫者羖羝勸西秦王乾歸稱籓於光，以子敕勃為質。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, King of Three Rivers Lü Guang led one hundred thousand men to attack Western Qin. Western Qin's Left Assistant Mi Gui Zhou and Left Guard General Mozhe Gudi urged Western Qin King Gangui to declare himself Guang's vassal and send his son Chibo as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, King of Three Rivers Lü Guang led one hundred thousand men against Western Qin. Western Qin's Left Assistant Mi Gui Zhou and Left Guard General Mozhe Gudi urged Gangui to submit to Guang and send his son Chibo as hostage.

sentences.zh: 光引兵還，乾歸悔之，殺周及羖羝。

translations.literal: Guang led his troops back; Gangui regretted it and killed Zhou and Gudi.
translations.idiomatic: Guang withdrew; Gangui regretted it and had Zhou and Gudi killed.

sentences.zh: 魏張兗聞燕軍將至，言於魏王珪曰：「燕狃於滑台、長子之捷，竭國之資力以來。

translations.literal: Wei Zhang Gun, hearing that Yan's army was about to arrive, said to Wei King Tuoba Gui: "Yan, accustomed to its victories at Huatai and Changzi, has exhausted the state's resources to come.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gun of Wei, hearing that Yan's army was approaching, said to Wei King Tuoba Gui, "Yan, emboldened by its victories at Huatai and Changzi, has exhausted the state's resources to come.

sentences.zh: 有輕我之心。

translations.literal: They have a mind to make light of us.
translations.idiomatic: They underestimate us.

sentences.zh: 宜羸形以驕之，乃可克也。」

translations.literal: We ought to show a weakened appearance to make them arrogant—only then can they be overcome."
translations.idiomatic: We should appear weak to make them arrogant—only then can we defeat them."

sentences.zh: 珪從之，悉徙部落畜產西渡河千餘里以避之。

translations.literal: Gui followed this, moved all tribes and livestock west across the river more than a thousand li to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Gui agreed and moved all tribes and livestock more than a thousand li west across the river to avoid them.

sentences.zh: 燕軍至五原，降魏別部三萬餘家，收穄田百餘萬斛，置黑城，進軍臨河，造船為濟具。

translations.literal: Yan's army reached Wuyuan, subdued Wei separate divisions of more than thirty thousand households, collected more than a million hu of millet fields, established Heicheng, advanced to Linhe, and built boats as crossing equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's army reached Wuyuan, reduced Wei detachments of more than thirty thousand households, gathered over a million hu of millet from the fields, established Black City, advanced to Linhe, and built boats for crossing the river.

sentences.zh: 珪遣右司馬許謙乞師於秦。

translations.literal: Gui sent Right Vice-Marshal Xu Qian to beg troops from Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui sent Right Vice-Marshal Xu Qian to Qin to request reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 禿髮烏孤擊乙弗、折掘等諸部，皆破降之，築廉川堡而都之。

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu attacked the tribes of Yifu, Zhejue, and others, all defeated and made to surrender, built Lianchuan Fort and made it his capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu attacked the Yifu, Zhejue, and other tribes, defeated them all and accepted their surrender, then built Lianchuan Fort and made it his capital.

sentences.zh: 廣武趙振，少好奇略，聞烏孤在廉川，棄家從之。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhen of Guangwu, from youth fond of unusual stratagems, heard Wugu was at Lianchuan, abandoned his family and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhen of Guangwu had been drawn to bold stratagems since youth; hearing that Wugu was at Lianchuan, he left his family and joined him.

sentences.zh: 烏孤喜曰：「吾得趙生，大事濟矣！」

translations.literal: Wugu said happily: "Having obtained Master Zhao, great affairs will succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Wugu said with delight, "With Master Zhao at my side, great things can be accomplished!"

sentences.zh: 拜左司馬。

translations.literal: He appointed him Left Vice-Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed him Left Vice-Marshal.

sentences.zh: 三河王光封烏孤為廣武郡公。

translations.literal: King of Three Rivers Lü Guang enfeoffed Wugu as Duke of Guangwu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: King of Three Rivers Lü Guang enfeoffed Wugu as Duke of Guangwu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 有長星見自須女，至於哭星。

translations.literal: A long comet appeared from Xunu and reached Kuxing.
translations.idiomatic: A long-tailed comet appeared, stretching from the Maiden constellation to the Weeping Star.

sentences.zh: 帝心惡之，於華林園舉酒祝之曰：「長星，勸汝一杯酒。

translations.literal: The Emperor's heart loathed it; in Hualin Garden he raised wine and toasted it, saying: "Long comet, I urge you to a cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took it as an ill omen. In Hualin Garden he raised a cup and toasted the comet: "Long comet, here is a cup of wine for you.

sentences.zh: 自古何有萬歲天子邪！」

translations.literal: Since antiquity, when has there ever been a ten-thousand-year Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, when has there ever been an emperor who lived ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 八月，魏王珪治兵河南。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Wei King Tuoba Gui trained troops south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wei King Tuoba Gui mustered his troops south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 九月，進軍臨河。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he advanced to Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, he advanced to Linhe.

sentences.zh: 燕太子寶列兵將濟，暴風起，漂其船數十艘洎南岸。

translations.literal: Yan Crown Prince Bao arrayed troops about to cross; a sudden storm arose and drifted dozens of their boats to the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Crown Prince Murong Bao drew up his troops to cross the river when a sudden storm arose and swept dozens of boats onto the south bank.

sentences.zh: 魏獲其甲士三百餘人，皆釋而遣之。

translations.literal: Wei captured more than three hundred of their armored soldiers, all released and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Wei captured more than three hundred armored soldiers and released them all.

sentences.zh: 寶之發中山也，燕主垂已有疾，既至五原，珪使人邀中山之路，伺其使者，盡執之，寶等數月不聞垂起居，珪使所執使者臨河告之曰：「若父已死，何不早歸！」

translations.literal: When Bao set out from Zhongshan, Yan ruler Chui was already ill. After reaching Wuyuan, Gui sent men to intercept the Zhongshan road, waited for their messengers, and seized them all. Bao and the others for several months heard nothing of Chui's daily condition. Gui had the seized messengers come to the river and tell them: "If your father is already dead, why not return early!"
translations.idiomatic: When Bao marched from Zhongshan, Yan ruler Murong Chui was already ill. After the Yan army reached Wuyuan, Tuoba Gui posted men along the road to Zhongshan, intercepted every messenger, and seized them. For months Bao heard nothing of Chui's condition. Gui then had the captured messengers come to the river and announce, "Your father is dead—why not return at once!"

sentences.zh: 寶等憂恐，士卒駭動。

translations.literal: Bao and the others were anxious and fearful; the soldiers were alarmed and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Bao and his officers were stricken with fear, and the troops were thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 珪使陳留公虔將五萬騎屯河東，東平公儀將十萬騎屯河北，略陽公遵將七萬騎塞燕軍之南。

translations.literal: Gui had Duke of Chenliu Qian lead fifty thousand cavalry stationed east of the river, Duke of Dongping Yi lead one hundred thousand cavalry stationed north of the river, and Duke of Lueyang Zun lead seventy thousand cavalry blocking south of the Yan army.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui posted Duke of Chenliu Qian with fifty thousand cavalry east of the river, Duke of Dongping Yi with one hundred thousand cavalry north of the river, and Duke of Lueyang Zun with seventy thousand cavalry to block the Yan army from the south.

sentences.zh: 遵，壽烏之子也。

translations.literal: Zun was the son of Shouwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was the son of Shouwu.

sentences.zh: 秦興遣楊佛嵩將兵救魏。

translations.literal: Qin ruler Xing sent Yang Fosong to lead troops to rescue Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin ruler Yao Xing sent Yang Fosong with an army to aid Wei.

sentences.zh: 燕術士靳安言於太子寶曰：「天時不利，燕必大敗，速去可免。」

translations.literal: Yan diviner Jin An said to Crown Prince Bao: "Heaven's timing is unfavorable; Yan is sure to suffer great defeat. Quick departure can avoid it."
translations.idiomatic: Yan diviner Jin An said to Crown Prince Bao, "The times are against us; Yan is doomed to a great defeat. Withdraw now and you may yet escape."

sentences.zh: 寶不聽。

translations.literal: Bao did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Bao refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 安退，告人曰：「吾輩皆當棄屍草野，不得歸矣！」

translations.literal: An withdrew and told others: "We all shall leave our corpses in the wild grass and will not be able to return!"
translations.idiomatic: An withdrew and told others, "We shall all leave our bones in the wild grass and never see home again!"

sentences.zh: 燕、魏相持積旬，趙王麟將慕輿嵩等以垂為實死，謀作亂，奉麟為主。

translations.literal: Yan and Wei faced off for many ten-day periods. Zhao Wang Lin led Murong Song and others, believing Chui was actually dead, plotted rebellion to set Lin up as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Wei remained locked in stalemate for weeks. Zhao Wang Murong Lin and Murong Song, believing Chui was truly dead, plotted a revolt to install Lin as ruler.

sentences.zh: 事洩，嵩等皆死，寶、麟等內自疑，冬，十月，辛未，燒船夜遁。

translations.literal: The affair leaked; Song and others all died. Bao, Lin, and others internally doubted each other. Winter, tenth month, xinwei, they burned boats and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was exposed; Song and his co-conspirators were executed. Bao, Lin, and the others grew suspicious of one another. In winter, the tenth month, on xinwei, they burned their boats and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 時河冰未結，寶以魏兵必不能渡，不設斥候。

translations.literal: At that time the river ice had not formed; Bao thought Wei troops surely could not cross and set no scouts.
translations.idiomatic: The river had not yet frozen, and Bao assumed the Wei army could not cross; he posted no scouts.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己卯，暴風，冰合。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, jimao, sudden storm, ice joined.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jimao, a sudden storm came and the river froze solid.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪引兵濟河，留輜重，選精銳二萬餘騎急追之。

translations.literal: Wei King Tuoba Gui led troops across the river, left baggage train, selected elite more than twenty thousand cavalry to pursue urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Wei King Tuoba Gui crossed the river with his army, left the baggage train behind, and chose more than twenty thousand elite cavalry to pursue in haste.

sentences.zh: 燕軍至參合陂，有大風，黑氣如堤，自軍後來，臨覆軍上。

translations.literal: Yan's army reached Canhe Marsh; there was strong wind, black vapor like an embankment coming from behind the army, looming over to cover the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army reached Canhe Marsh, a fierce wind arose and black vapor like an earthen dike rolled in from the rear, threatening to engulf the whole force.

sentences.zh: 沙門支曇猛言於寶曰：「風氣暴迅，魏兵將至之候，宜遣兵御之。」

translations.literal: Monk Zhi Tanmeng said to Bao: "The wind is violently swift—a sign Wei troops are about to arrive. We ought to send troops to defend against them."
translations.idiomatic: The monk Zhi Tanmeng said to Bao, "This violent wind is a sign that Wei troops are near. You should send men to meet them."

sentences.zh: 寶以去魏軍已遠，笑而不應。

translations.literal: Bao, thinking they were already far from Wei's army, laughed and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Bao, believing the Wei army was already far behind, only laughed and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 曇猛固請不已，麟怒曰：「以殿下神武，師徒之盛，足以橫行沙漠，索虜何敢遠來！

translations.literal: Tanmeng repeatedly pressed without stopping; Lin angrily said: "With Your Highness's divine martial prowess and the army's abundance, enough to march freely across the desert—how dare the Suo barbarians come from afar!
translations.idiomatic: Tanmeng pressed his warning again and again until Lin burst out in anger: "With Your Highness's martial brilliance and this mighty army, we can sweep across the desert at will—how dare those northern barbarians come so far!

sentences.zh: 而曇猛妄言驚眾，當斬以徇！」

translations.literal: Yet Tanmeng speaks wild words to alarm the masses—he should be beheaded to display!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tanmeng spreads false alarms among the troops—he ought to be beheaded as an example!"

sentences.zh: 曇猛泣曰：「苻氏以百萬之師，敗於淮南，正由恃眾輕敵，不信天道故也！」

translations.literal: Tanmeng wept and said: "The Fu clan with an army of a million was defeated at Huainan—precisely because they relied on numbers and slighted the enemy, not believing Heaven's Way!"
translations.idiomatic: Tanmeng wept and said, "The Fu clan marched a million men and was crushed at Huainan—precisely because they trusted in numbers, despised their foe, and refused to heed Heaven's will!"

sentences.zh: 司徒德勸寶從曇猛言，寶乃遣麟帥騎三萬居軍後以備非常。

translations.literal: Minister of Education De urged Bao to follow Tanmeng's words; Bao then sent Lin leading thirty thousand cavalry to stay at the army rear to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Murong De urged Bao to heed Tanmeng; Bao then sent Lin with thirty thousand cavalry to hold the rear against any surprise.

sentences.zh: 麟以曇猛赤妄，縱騎遊獵，不肯設備。

translations.literal: Lin, considering Tanmeng alarmist and false, let cavalry roam hunting and was unwilling to set defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Lin dismissed Tanmeng as a panic-monger, let his horsemen roam on hunts, and refused to prepare any defense.

sentences.zh: 寶遣騎還詗魏兵，騎和十餘里，即解鞍寢。

translations.literal: Bao sent cavalry back to scout Wei's army; the cavalry had gone only ten-odd li when they unbridled and slept.
translations.idiomatic: Bao sent cavalry back to reconnoiter the Wei army, but after barely ten li they unsaddled their horses and went to sleep.

sentences.zh: 魏軍晨夜兼行，乙酉，暮，至參合陂西。

translations.literal: Wei's army marched day and night together; yiyou, at dusk, reached west of Canhe Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army marched day and night without rest; on yiyou, at dusk, they reached the west side of Canhe Marsh.

sentences.zh: 燕軍在陂東，營於蟠羊山南水上。

translations.literal: Yan's army was east of the marsh, encamped south of the water at Panyang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army was east of the marsh, encamped on the south bank below Panyang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪夜部分諸將，掩覆燕軍，士卒銜枚束馬口潛進。

translations.literal: Wei King Tuoba Gui at night assigned the generals to envelop and cover the Yan army; soldiers held wooden gags in their mouths, tied horse mouths, and advanced secretly.
translations.idiomatic: That night Wei King Tuoba Gui deployed his generals to surround the Yan camp; the men marched with gags in their mouths and their horses' muzzles bound.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，日出，魏軍登山，下臨燕營。

translations.literal: Bingxu, at sunrise, Wei's army ascended the mountain and looked down on the Yan camp.
translations.idiomatic: At sunrise on bingxu the Wei army climbed the heights and looked down on the Yan encampment.

sentences.zh: 燕軍將東引，顧見之，士卒大驚擾亂。

translations.literal: Yan's army was about to march east; looking back they saw them; the soldiers were greatly alarmed and thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army was about to march east when they looked back and saw the Wei host; the troops were thrown into terror and chaos.

sentences.zh: 珪縱兵擊之，燕兵走赴水，人馬相騰，躡壓溺死者以萬數。

translations.literal: Gui released troops to attack; Yan soldiers fled toward the water; men and horses trampled each other; treading and drowning deaths numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui unleashed his attack; Yan soldiers fled into the water, men and horses trampling one another; tens of thousands were crushed or drowned.

sentences.zh: 略陽公遵以兵邀其前，燕兵四五萬人，一時放仗斂手就禽，其遺迸去者不過數千人，太子寶等皆單騎僅免。

translations.literal: Duke of Lueyang Zun with troops intercepted their front; forty or fifty thousand Yan soldiers at once dropped weapons, folded hands, and were captured; those who scattered and fled were no more than a few thousand; Crown Prince Bao and others all escaped barely on single horses.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Lueyang Zun blocked their path with troops; forty or fifty thousand Yan soldiers at once dropped their weapons and surrendered; only a few thousand escaped; Crown Prince Bao and the other leaders fled alone on single horses with their lives barely spared.

sentences.zh: 殺燕右僕陳留悼王紹，生禽魯陽王倭奴、桂林王道成、濟陰公尹國等文武將吏數千人，兵甲糧貨以巨萬計。

translations.literal: They killed Yan's Right Deputy, Mourning King of Chenliu Shao; captured alive Luoyang Wang Wonu, Guilin Wang Daocheng, Duke of Jiyin Yin Guo, and civil and military officers numbering thousands; arms, armor, grain, and goods counted in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Yan's Right Deputy, Mourning King of Chenliu Murong Shao, and took alive Luoyang Wang Wonu, Guilin Wang Murong Daocheng, Duke of Jiyin Yin Guo, and thousands of civil and military officers, along with arms, armor, grain, and goods beyond count.

sentences.zh: 道成，垂之弟子也。

translations.literal: Daocheng was Chui's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng was a nephew of Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪擇燕臣之有才用者代郡太守廣川賈閏、閏從弟驃騎長史昌黎太守彝、太史郎遼東晁崇等留之，其餘欲悉給衣糧遣還，以招懷中州之人。

translations.literal: Wei King Tuoba Gui selected capable Yan ministers—Guangchuan Jia Run, Governor of Dai Commandery; Run's younger male cousin Yi, Chief of Staff to the Cavalry General and Governor of Changli; Chaoyang Chao Chong of Liaodong, Clerk of the Grand Astrologer—and kept them; the rest he wished to all provide clothing and grain and send back, to win over the people of the Central Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Wei King Tuoba Gui kept the ablest Yan officials—Jia Run of Guangchuan, Governor of Dai Commandery; Run's cousin Yi, chief of staff to the Cavalry General and Governor of Changli; and Chao Chong of Liaodong, clerk of the Grand Astrologer—and planned to clothe and feed the rest and send them home to win over the people of the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 中部大人王建曰：「燕眾強盛，今傾國而來，我幸而大捷，不如悉殺之，則其國空虛，取之為易。

translations.literal: Central Chieftain Wang Jian said: "Yan's masses are strong and flourishing; now they have come with the whole state; we were fortunate and won greatly—better to kill them all, then their state will be empty and taking it will be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Central Chieftain Wang Jian said, "Yan is strong; they came with the whole nation, and we were lucky to win so decisively. Better kill them all—their state will be hollowed out and easy to take.

sentences.zh: 且獲寇而縱之，無乃不可乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, to capture enemies and then release them—is that not impermissible!"
translations.idiomatic: And to capture foes only to let them go—surely that is unwise!"

sentences.zh: 乃盡坑之。

translations.literal: Then they buried them all alive.
translations.idiomatic: Then they buried them all alive.

sentences.zh: 十二月，珪還雲中盛樂。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Gui returned to Shengle in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Tuoba Gui returned to Shengle in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 燕太子寶恥於參合之敗，請更擊魏。

translations.literal: Yan Crown Prince Bao, shamed by the Canhe defeat, requested to attack Wei again.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Crown Prince Murong Bao, shamed by the defeat at Canhe, asked to strike Wei again.

sentences.zh: 司徒德言於燕主垂曰：「虜以參合之捷，有輕太子之心，宜及陛下神略以服之，不然，將為後患。」

translations.literal: Minister of Education De said to Yan ruler Chui: "The enemy, because of the Canhe victory, has a mind to make light of the crown prince—we ought to take advantage of Your Majesty's divine strategy to subdue them; otherwise they will become a later trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Murong De said to Yan ruler Chui, "The enemy, emboldened by Canhe, now despises the crown prince. Your Majesty should strike while your genius still commands awe, or Wei will become a lasting threat."

sentences.zh: 垂乃以清河公會錄留台事，領幽州刺史，代高陽王隆鎮龍城；

translations.literal: Chui then had Duke of Qinghe Hui record remaining court affairs, serve as Inspector of You Province, replacing Gaoyang Wang Long as garrison at Longcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Chui then put Duke of Qinghe Murong Hui in charge of the remaining court business as Inspector of You Province, replacing Gaoyang Wang Murong Long as garrison commander at Longcheng;

sentences.zh: 以陽城王蘭汗為北中郎將，代長樂公盛鎮薊；

translations.literal: had Yangcheng Wang Lanhan as North General of the Gentlemen, replacing Duke of Changle Sheng as garrison at Ji;
translations.idiomatic: made Yangcheng Wang Lanhan North General of the Gentlemen, replacing Duke of Changle Murong Sheng as garrison commander at Ji;

sentences.zh: 命隆、盛悉引其精兵還中山，期以明年大舉擊魏。

translations.literal: ordered Long and Sheng to all lead their elite troops back to Zhongshan, planning next year a great campaign against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered Long and Sheng to bring all their elite troops back to Zhongshan, planning a major campaign against Wei the following year.

sentences.zh: 是歲，秦主興封其叔父緒為晉王，碩德為隴西王，弟崇為齊公，顯為常山公。

translations.literal: That year, Qin ruler Xing enfeoffed his uncle Xu as King of Jin, Shuode as King of Longxi, younger brother Chong as Duke of Qi, and Xian as Duke of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qin ruler Yao Xing enfeoffed his uncle Yao Xu as King of Jin, Yao Shuode as King of Longxi, his younger brother Yao Chong as Duke of Qi, and Yao Xian as Duke of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝下太元二十一年

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong, the twenty-first year of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of the Liezong: the twenty-first year of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，燕高陽王隆引龍城之甲入中山，軍容精整，燕人之氣稍振。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, Yan Gaoyang Wang Long led Longcheng armored troops into Zhongshan; military appearance refined and orderly; Yan people's morale slightly revived.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Yan Gaoyang Wang Murong Long led the armored troops from Longcheng into Zhongshan; their bearing was sharp and disciplined, and Yan morale revived a little.

sentences.zh: 休官權萬世帥眾降西秦。

translations.literal: Xiuguan Quan Wanshi led his followers to surrender to Western Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuguan Quan Wanshi led his followers in surrender to Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂遣征東將軍平規發兵冀州。

translations.literal: Yan ruler Chui sent Eastern Campaign General Ping Gui to mobilize troops in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ruler Murong Chui sent Eastern Campaign General Ping Gui to raise troops in Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 二月，規以博陵、武邑、長樂三郡兵反於魯口，其從子冀州刺史喜諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Second month, Gui rebelled at Lukou with troops of Boling, Wuyi, and Changle commanderies; his nephew Xi, Inspector of Ji Province, remonstrated—he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Gui rebelled at Lukou with the forces of Boling, Wuyi, and Changle commanderies; his nephew Xi, Inspector of Ji Province, remonstrated with him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 規弟海陽令翰亦起兵於遼西以應之。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brother Han, Magistrate of Haiyang, also raised troops in Liaoxi in response.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger brother Han, magistrate of Haiyang, also raised troops in Liaoxi in support.

sentences.zh: 垂遣鎮東將軍餘嵩擊規，嵩敗死。

translations.literal: Chui sent Eastern Garrison General Yu Song to attack Gui; Song was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Chui sent Eastern Garrison General Yu Song against Gui; Song was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 垂自將擊規，軍至魯口，規棄眾，將妻子及平喜等數十人走渡河，垂引兵還。

translations.literal: Chui personally led an attack on Gui; the army reached Lukou; Gui abandoned his troops, took wife, children, and Ping Xi and dozens of others, fled crossing the river; Chui led troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Chui marched in person against Gui; when his army reached Lukou, Gui abandoned his forces, took his wife, children, Ping Xi, and a few dozen followers, and fled across the river; Chui then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 翰引兵趣龍城，清河公會遣東陽公根等擊翰，破之，翰走山南。

translations.literal: Han led troops toward Longcheng; Duke of Qinghe Hui sent Dongyang Duke Gen and others to attack Han, defeated him; Han fled south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Han marched on Longcheng; Duke of Qinghe Murong Hui sent Dongyang Duke Murong Gen and others against him, routed him, and Han fled south of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚子，燕主垂留范陽王德守中山，引兵密發。

translations.literal: Third month, gengzi, Yan ruler Chui left Fanyang Wang De to guard Zhongshan and led troops secretly dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengzi, Yan ruler Murong Chui left Fanyang Wang Murong De to hold Zhongshan and set out in secret.

sentences.zh: 逾青嶺，經天門，鑿山通道，出魏不意，直指雲中。

translations.literal: Crossed Qing Ridge, passed Heaven Gate, cut through mountains to open a path, caught Wei unawares, pointed straight at Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed Qing Ridge, passed through Heaven Gate, cut a road through the mountains, caught Wei off guard, and drove straight for Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 魏陳留公虔帥部落三萬餘家鎮平城；

translations.literal: Wei Duke of Chenliu Qian commanded tribes of more than thirty thousand households garrisoning Pingcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Duke of Chenliu Qian held Pingcheng with more than thirty thousand tribal households;

sentences.zh: 垂至獵嶺，以遼西王農、高陽王隆為前鋒以襲之。

translations.literal: Chui reached Lie Ridge, used Liaoxi Wang Nong and Gaoyang Wang Long as vanguard to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chui reached Lie Ridge, he sent Liaoxi Wang Murong Nong and Gaoyang Wang Murong Long as vanguard to strike Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 是時，燕兵新敗，皆畏魏，惟龍城兵勇銳爭先。

translations.literal: At this time Yan troops newly defeated all feared Wei; only Longcheng troops were brave and sharp, competing to lead.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Yan army, fresh from defeat, feared Wei; only the troops from Longcheng were bold and eager to fight.

sentences.zh: 虔素不設備，閏月，乙卯，燕軍至平城，虔乃覺之，帥麾下出戰，敗死，燕軍盡收其部落。

translations.literal: Qian from of old set no defenses; intercalary month, yimao, Yan army reached Pingcheng; Qian then noticed, led his followers out to battle, was defeated and died; Yan army fully collected his tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had long neglected his defenses; in the intercalary month, on yimao, the Yan army reached Pingcheng before he realized what was happening. He led his followers out to fight, was defeated and killed, and the Yan army absorbed all his tribes.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪震怖，欲走，諸部聞虔死，皆有貳心，珪不知所適。

translations.literal: Wei King Tuoba Gui was shaken and terrified, wished to flee; all tribes hearing Qian died all had hearts of disloyalty; Gui did not know where to go.
translations.idiomatic: Wei King Tuoba Gui was shaken with terror and thought of flight; when the tribes heard of Qian's death, many wavered in loyalty, and Gui did not know where to turn.

sentences.zh: 垂之過參合陂也，見積骸如山，為之設祭，軍士皆慟哭，聲震山谷。

translations.literal: When Chui passed Canhe Marsh, he saw piled bones like mountains; for them he set up sacrifice; soldiers all wailed; sound shook mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When Chui passed Canhe Marsh and saw bones heaped like mountains, he offered sacrifice for the dead; the soldiers wailed until the sound shook the valleys.

sentences.zh: 垂慚憤嘔血，由是發疾，乘馬輿而進，頓平城西北三十里。

translations.literal: Chui ashamed and furious vomited blood; from this illness arose; rode in horse-drawn litter and advanced; halted thirty li northwest of Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chui, shamed and enraged, vomited blood and fell ill; he continued in a horse-drawn litter and halted thirty li northwest of Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 太子寶等聞之，皆引還。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Bao and others hearing this, all led back.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Bao and the others heard of it, they all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 燕軍叛者告於魏云「垂已死，輿屍在軍。」

translations.literal: Yan army deserters told Wei saying "Chui is already dead; the litter carries a corpse in the army."
translations.idiomatic: Yan deserters told Wei, "Chui is dead; the army is carrying his corpse in a litter."

sentences.zh: 魏王珪欲追之，聞平城已沒，乃引還阻山。

translations.literal: Wei King Tuoba Gui wished to pursue; hearing Pingcheng had fallen, then led back to obstructing mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui wanted to pursue, but when he heard Pingcheng had fallen he withdrew into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 垂在平城積十日，疾轉篤，乃築燕昌城而還。

translations.literal: Chui at Pingcheng accumulated ten days; illness turned severe; then built Yanchang City and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chui remained at Pingcheng ten days, but his illness worsened; he built Yanchang City and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸未，卒於上谷之沮陽，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, guiwei, died at Juyang in Shanggu; secretly did not announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guiwei, he died at Juyang in Shanggu; mourning was kept secret.

sentences.zh: 丙申，至中山；

translations.literal: Bingshen, arrived at Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the procession reached Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 戊戌，發喪，謚曰成武皇帝，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: Wuxu, announced mourning; posthumous title Emperor Chengwu; temple name Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu mourning was announced; he was posthumously titled Emperor Chengwu and given the temple name Shizu.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，太子寶即位，大赦，改元永康。

translations.literal: Renyin, Crown Prince Bao took the throne; great amnesty; changed era to Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Crown Prince Bao ascended the throne, declared a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛亥，以范陽王德為都督冀、兗、青、徐、荊、豫六州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、冀州牧，鎮鄴；

translations.literal: Fifth month, xinhai, made Fanyang Wang De Commander of All Military Affairs for the six provinces Ji, Yan, Qing, Xu, Jing, and Yu; General of Chariots and Cavalry; Governor of Ji Province; garrisoned at Ye;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinhai, Fanyang Wang Murong De was made commander of all military affairs for Ji, Yan, Qing, Xu, Jing, and Yu; General of Chariots and Cavalry; Governor of Ji Province; and garrisoned at Ye;

sentences.zh: 遼西王農為都督并、雍、益、梁、秦、涼六州諸軍事、并州牧，鎮晉陽。

translations.literal: Liaoxi Wang Nong as Commander of All Military Affairs for the six provinces Bing, Yong, Yi, Liang, Qin, and Liang; Governor of Bing Province; garrisoned at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoxi Wang Murong Nong was made commander of all military affairs for Bing, Yong, Yi, Liang, Qin, and Liang; Governor of Bing Province; and garrisoned at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 又以安定王庫辱官偉為太師，夫餘王為太傅。

translations.literal: Also made Prince of Anding Kuruguan Wei Grand Preceptor and Prince of Fuyu Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Kuruguan Wei, Prince of Anding, was made Grand Preceptor, and the Prince of Fuyu was made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以趙王麟領尚書左僕射，高陽王隆領右僕射，長樂公盛為司隸校尉，宜都王鳳為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Jiayin, made Zhao Wang Lin oversee Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Gaoyang Wang Long Right Vice Director; Duke of Changle Sheng Colonel Director of Retainers; Prince of Yidu Feng Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Zhao Wang Murong Lin was put in charge of the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Gaoyang Wang Murong Long the Right Vice Director; Duke of Changle Murong Sheng Colonel Director of Retainers; and Prince of Yidu Murong Feng Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以散騎常侍彭城劉該為徐州刺史，鎮鄄城。

translations.literal: Yimao, made Regular Palace Attendant Liu Gai of Pengcheng Inspector of Xu Province; garrisoned at Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Regular Palace Attendant Liu Gai of Pengcheng was made Inspector of Xu Province and garrisoned at Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以望蔡公謝琰為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Jiazi, made Duke of Wangcai Xie Yan Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Duke of Wangcai Xie Yan was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 初，燕主垂先段后生子令、寶，後段后生子朗、鑒，愛諸姬子麟、農、隆、柔、熙。

translations.literal: Initially, Yan ruler Chui's former Empress Duan bore sons Ling and Bao; later Empress Duan bore sons Lang and Jian; he loved various concubines' sons Lin, Nong, Long, Rou, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yan ruler Murong Chui's first Empress Duan had borne sons Ling and Bao; his later Empress Duan bore Lang and Jian; and he favored the sons of his concubines—Lin, Nong, Long, Rou, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 寶初為太子，有美稱，已而荒怠，中外失望。

translations.literal: Bao at first as crown prince had fine reputation; afterward became negligent and idle; inside and outside disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao was first made crown prince he had a fine reputation, but later he grew negligent and idle, and court and country alike lost hope in him.

sentences.zh: 後段后嘗言於垂曰：「太子遭承平之世，足為守成之主；

translations.literal: Later Empress Duan once said to Chui: "The crown prince, meeting a time of enduring peace, is sufficient to be a ruler who preserves accomplishments;
translations.idiomatic: Later Empress Duan once said to Chui, "In a time of peace the crown prince would be enough to preserve what has been won;

sentences.zh: 今國步艱難，恐非濟世之才。

translations.literal: now the state's step is difficult—we fear he is not talent to rescue the age.
translations.idiomatic: but the realm is in peril now, and I fear he is not the man to save it.

sentences.zh: 遼西、高陽二王，陛下之賢子，宜擇一人，付以大業。

translations.literal: Liaoxi and Gaoyang two kings—Your Majesty's worthy sons—one ought to be chosen and entrusted with the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaoxi and Gaoyang kings are worthy sons of Your Majesty; one of them should be chosen and entrusted with the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 趙王麟奸詐強愎，異日必為國家之患，宜早圖之。」

translations.literal: Zhao Wang Lin is treacherous, deceitful, stubborn and wilful; another day he is sure to become the state's trouble—we ought early to plan against him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wang Lin is treacherous and obstinate; one day he will surely become a danger to the state, and you should deal with him early."

sentences.zh: 寶善事垂左右，左右多譽之，故垂以為賢，謂段氏曰：「汝欲使我為晉獻公乎？」

translations.literal: Bao well served Chui's attendants; attendants much praised him; therefore Chui considered him worthy and said to Lady Duan: "Do you wish to make me Duke Xian of Jin?"
translations.idiomatic: Bao had cultivated Chui's attendants, and they praised him lavishly, so Chui thought him worthy and said to Lady Duan, "Do you want to make me into Duke Xian of Jin?"

sentences.zh: 段氏泣而退，告其妹范陽王妃曰：「太子不才，天下所知，吾為社稷言之，主上乃以吾為驪姬，何其苦哉！

translations.literal: Lady Duan wept and withdrew, told her younger sister the Princess of Fanyang: "The crown prince lacks talent—all under Heaven knows it. I spoke for the altars of soil and grain; the sovereign yet took me for Li Ji—how bitter!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Duan withdrew in tears and told her younger sister, the Princess of Fanyang, "The crown prince's inadequacy is known to all. I spoke for the sake of the realm, yet the sovereign treats me like Li Ji—how bitter this is!

sentences.zh: 觀太子必喪社稷，范陽王有非常器度，若燕祚未盡，其在王乎！」

translations.literal: Observing, the crown prince is sure to lose the altars of soil and grain; Fanyang Wang has extraordinary capacity—if Yan's fortune is not yet exhausted, is it not in the Wang!"
translations.idiomatic: I can see the crown prince will ruin the state. Fanyang Wang has uncommon stature—if Yan's fortune is not yet spent, surely it rests with him!"

sentences.zh: 寶及麟聞而恨之。

translations.literal: Bao and Lin heard and resented it.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao and Lin heard this, they hated her for it.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，使麟謂段氏曰：「后常謂主上不能守大業，今竟能不？

translations.literal: On yichou, sent Lin to tell Lady Duan: "The empress often said the sovereign could not preserve the great enterprise—can he now or not?
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day, Bao sent Lin to tell Lady Duan, "The empress often said our lord could not hold the realm together—has she been proved wrong?

sentences.zh: 宜早自裁，以全段宗！」

translations.literal: You ought early to take your own life, to preserve the Duan clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Take your own life soon, while you still can save the Duan line!"

sentences.zh: 段氏怒曰：「汝兄弟不難逼殺其母，況能守先業乎！

translations.literal: Lady Duan angrily said: "Your brothers would not find it hard to force your mother to death—how much less can you preserve the ancestral enterprise!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Duan flared up. "Your brothers had no trouble driving your mother to her death—what hope is there that you can guard our fathers' legacy?

sentences.zh: 吾豈愛死，但念國亡不久耳。」

translations.literal: I—how would I cherish death? I only think the state will perish before long."
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I cling to life—I only see the kingdom falling apart before my eyes."

sentences.zh: 遂自殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon she killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: With that she took her own life.

sentences.zh: 寶議以段后謀廢適統，無母后之道，不宜成喪，群臣咸以為然。

translations.literal: Bao proposed that because Empress Duan plotted to depose the legitimate succession, lacking the way of an empress dowager, she should not receive full mourning; all ministers agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Bao argued that Empress Duan had schemed to overturn the rightful succession and had failed the duties of an empress dowager, so she ought not receive full mourning rites. The ministers all agreed.

sentences.zh: 中書令眭邃揚言於朝曰：「子無廢母之義，漢安恩閻后親廢順帝，猶得配饗太廟，況先后暖昧之言，虛實未可知乎？」

translations.literal: Chief Secretary Suixuan proclaimed at court: "A son has no principle of deposing his mother. Empress Yan En of Han An personally deposed Emperor Shun, yet still received offerings in the Grand Temple—how much more when the former empress's words were ambiguous, and truth and falsehood cannot yet be known?"
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretary Suixuan declared openly at court, "No son may cast off his mother. Empress Yan En of Han An personally set aside Emperor Shun, yet still shared offerings in the Grand Temple—how much less may we judge a former empress on vague words whose truth is still unknown?"

sentences.zh: 乃成喪。

translations.literal: Full mourning was then performed.
translations.idiomatic: Full mourning was carried out after all.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸酉，魏王珪遣將軍王建等擊燕廣寧太守劉亢泥，斬之，徙其部落於平城。

translations.literal: Sixth month, guiyou, Wei King Gui sent General Wang Jian and others to attack Yan's Administrator of Guangning Liu Kangni, beheaded him, and moved his tribe to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guiyou, Wei King Tuoba Gui sent General Wang Jian and others against Liu Kangni, Administrator of Guangning under Yan. They killed him and resettled his people at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 燕上谷太守開封公詳棄郡走。

translations.literal: Yan's Administrator of Shanggu, Duke of Kaifeng Xiang, abandoned the commandery and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, Duke of Kaifeng and Administrator of Shanggu under Yan, abandoned his commandery and fled.

sentences.zh: 詳，之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Xiang was Gui's great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was a great-grandson of Gui.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏賀太妃卒。

translations.literal: Dinghai, Wei Consort He died.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Consort He of Wei died.

sentences.zh: 燕主寶定士族舊籍，分辨清濁，校閱戶口，罷軍營封廕之戶，悉屬郡縣。

translations.literal: Yan ruler Bao fixed the old registers of gentry families, distinguished pure from impure, checked household registers, abolished households with military-camp hereditary privileges, and made all belong to commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao fixed the old registers of the gentry, sorted families into pure and impure ranks, audited household rolls, and abolished the privileged households tied to military camps, placing them all under civil commandery and county administration.

sentences.zh: 由是士民嗟怨，始有離心。

translations.literal: From this gentry and commoners sighed in resentment and first had hearts of separation.
translations.idiomatic: From this the gentry and common people groaned in anger, and loyalty began to fray.

sentences.zh: 三河王呂光即天王位，國號大涼，大赦，改元龍飛。

translations.literal: Three Rivers King Lü Guang took the Heavenly King throne; state name Great Liang; great amnesty; changed era to Longfei.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang, King of Three Rivers, ascended the throne as Heavenly King, named his state Great Liang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Longfei.

sentences.zh: 備置百官，以世子紹為太子，封子弟為公侯者二十人，以中書令王詳為尚書左僕射，著作郎段業等五人為尚書。

translations.literal: Fully established the hundred offices; made heir Shao crown prince; enfeoffed younger brothers and sons as dukes and marquises, twenty men; made Chief Secretary Wang Xiang Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; made Editorial Director Duan Ye and five others Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He fully staffed the bureaucracy, named his heir Shao crown prince, and enfeoffed twenty younger kinsmen as dukes and marquises. Wang Xiang, Chief Secretary, became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Duan Ye and four other Editorial Directors were made Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 光遣使者拜禿髮烏孤為征南大將軍、益州牧、左賢王。

translations.literal: Guang sent envoys to appoint Tufa Wugu General Who Conquers the South, Governor of Yi Province, and Left Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang sent envoys to invest Tufa Wugu as General Who Conquers the South, Governor of Yi Province, and Left Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 烏孤謂使者曰：「呂王諸子貪淫，三甥暴虐，遠近愁怨，吾安可違百姓之心，受不義之爵乎？

translations.literal: Wugu said to the envoys: "King Lü's sons are greedy and licentious; three nephews are cruel and tyrannical; near and far groan in resentment—how could I go against the people's hearts and accept an unrighteous rank?
translations.idiomatic: Wugu told the envoys, "King Lü's sons are greedy and debauched, his three nephews brutal and cruel, and resentment runs deep far and near. How could I defy the people's will and accept an unearned title?

sentences.zh: 吾當為帝王之事耳。」

translations.literal: I ought to do the affairs of emperor and king, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: I mean to do the work of an emperor myself."

sentences.zh: 乃留其鼓吹、羽儀，謝而遣之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he kept their music and feather banners, declined, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He kept their ceremonial musicians and banners, politely refused the appointment, and sent the envoys home.

sentences.zh: 平規收合餘黨據高唐，燕主寶遣高陽王隆將兵討之。

translations.literal: Ping Gui gathered remaining partisans and held Gaotang; Yan ruler Bao sent Gaoyang Wang Long to lead troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Gui rallied the remnants of his faction and seized Gaotang. Murong Bao sent Gaoyang Wang Long at the head of an army to crush him.

sentences.zh: 東土之民，素懷隆惠，迎候者屬路。

translations.literal: The people of the eastern lands, who long cherished Long's kindness, welcomed him in unbroken lines along the road.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the eastern provinces had long benefited from Long's kindness, and crowds lined the roads to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，隆進軍臨河，規棄高唐走。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Long advanced the army to the river; Gui abandoned Gaotang and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Long marched to the river. Gui abandoned Gaotang and fled.

sentences.zh: 隆遣建威將軍慕容進等濟河追之，斬規於濟北。

translations.literal: Long sent General Who Establishes Might Murong Jin and others to cross the river in pursuit and beheaded Gui north of the Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Long sent Murong Jin, General Who Establishes Might, and others across the river in pursuit and killed Gui north of the Ji.

sentences.zh: 平喜奔彭城。

translations.literal: Ping Xi fled to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Xi fled to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 納故中書令王獻之女為太子妃。

translations.literal: Took the daughter of former Chief Secretary Wang Xian as crown prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince took as his consort the daughter of the late Chief Secretary Wang Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 獻之，羲之之子也。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was Xizhi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was a son of the calligrapher Wang Xizhi.

sentences.zh: 魏群臣勸魏王珪稱尊號，珪始建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，改元皇始。

translations.literal: Wei ministers urged Wei King Gui to assume an exalted title; Gui first established the Son of Heaven's banners, went out and in with imperial guard, and changed era to Huangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ministers urged King Tuoba Gui to take an imperial title. He first raised the imperial banners, traveled with the full panoply of imperial escort, and changed the era name to Huangshi.

sentences.zh: 參軍事上谷張恂勸珪進取中原，珪善之。

translations.literal: Staff Officer Zhang Xun of Shanggu urged Gui to advance and seize the Central Plains; Gui approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun of Shanggu, a staff officer, urged Gui to push into the Central Plains, and Gui welcomed the advice.

sentences.zh: 燕遼西王農悉將部曲數萬口之并州，并州素乏儲郞。

translations.literal: Yan Liaoxi Wang Nong entirely led his personal forces, tens of thousands, to Bing Province; Bing Province had long lacked stored grain.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong, Liaoxi Wang of Yan, moved his entire personal following of tens of thousands into Bing Province, which had always been short of stored grain.

sentences.zh: 是歲早霜，民不能供其食。

translations.literal: That year early frost came; the people could not supply their food.
translations.idiomatic: That year an early frost ruined the harvest, and the people could not feed them.

sentences.zh: 又遣諸部護軍分監諸胡，由是民夷俱怨，潛召魏軍。

translations.literal: Also sent protective generals of various departments to divide supervision over the various Hu; from this Han and non-Han alike resented, and secretly summoned Wei troops.
translations.idiomatic: He also posted departmental protective generals to keep watch over the non-Han peoples, and resentment spread among both Han and non-Han alike until they began secretly inviting Wei forces in.

sentences.zh: 八月，己亥，魏王珪大舉伐燕，步騎四十餘萬，南出馬邑，逾句注，旌旗二千餘里，鼓行而進。

translations.literal: Eighth month, jihai, Wei King Gui launched a great campaign against Yan—infantry and cavalry over four hundred thousand—marched south from Mayi, crossed Gouzhu; banners and flags stretched over two thousand li; advanced beating drums.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jihai, Wei King Gui launched a massive invasion of Yan with more than four hundred thousand infantry and cavalry. They marched south from Mayi, crossed Gouzhu Pass, and advanced in a column of banners two thousand li long, drums beating all the way.

sentences.zh: 左將軍雁門李栗將五萬騎為前驅，別遣將國封真等從東道出軍都，襲燕幽州。

translations.literal: Left General Li Li of Yanmen led fifty thousand cavalry as vanguard; separately sent General Guo Fengzhen and others by the eastern route out through Jundu to strike Yan's You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Left General Li Li of Yanmen led fifty thousand horsemen as the vanguard, while Guo Fengzhen and other generals were sent separately by the eastern route through Jundu to strike at Yan's You Province.

sentences.zh: 燕征北大將軍、幽、平二州牧、清河公會母賤而年長，雄俊有器藝，燕主垂愛之。

translations.literal: Yan General Who Conquers the North, Governor of You and Ping provinces, Duke of Qinghe Hui—his mother was lowly yet he was eldest; heroic and handsome, with capacity and skill; Yan ruler Chui loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui, General Who Conquers the North, Governor of You and Ping, and Duke of Qinghe, was born of a humble mother yet was the eldest son—bold, handsome, and gifted. Murong Chui doted on him.

sentences.zh: 寶之伐魏也，垂命會攝東宮事、總錄，禮遇一如太子。

translations.literal: When Bao attacked Wei, Chui ordered Hui to administer Eastern Palace affairs and general oversight; courtesy and treatment exactly like the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao marched against Wei, Chui put Hui in charge of Eastern Palace affairs and overall administration, treating him with all the honors due a crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及垂代魏，命會鎮龍城，委以東北之任，國官府佐，皆選一時才望。

translations.literal: When Chui replaced Wei, he ordered Hui to garrison Longcheng and entrusted him with the northeast mission; state and government aides were all chosen from the talent and repute of the age.
translations.idiomatic: When Chui campaigned against Wei in person, he left Hui to hold Longcheng and entrusted him with the whole northeast, staffing his administration with the finest men of the day.

sentences.zh: 垂疾篤，遺言命寶以會為嗣；

translations.literal: Chui's illness turned grave; his final words ordered Bao to make Hui successor;
translations.idiomatic: As Chui lay dying, his last instruction was that Bao should make Hui his heir;

sentences.zh: 而寶愛少子濮陽公策，意不在會。

translations.literal: but Bao loved his younger son Duke of Puyang Ce; his mind was not on Hui.
translations.idiomatic: but Bao favored his younger son Murong Ce, Duke of Puyang, and his heart was set elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 長樂公盛與會同年，恥為之下，乃與趙王麟共勸寶立策，寶從之。

translations.literal: Duke of Changle Sheng was the same age as Hui and ashamed to be beneath him; then with Zhao Wang Lin jointly urged Bao to establish Ce; Bao followed.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, Duke of Changle, was Hui's age and resented ranking below him. He joined Zhao Wang Lin in urging Bao to name Ce heir, and Bao agreed.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，立妃段氏為皇后，策為皇太子，會、盛皆進爵為王。

translations.literal: Yihai, established Consort Duan as empress, Ce as crown prince; Hui and Sheng both advanced in rank to kings.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Consort Duan was made empress and Ce crown prince, while Hui and Sheng were both promoted to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 策年十一，素憃弱；

translations.literal: Ce was eleven years old, by nature dull and weak;
translations.idiomatic: Ce was only eleven and naturally timid and frail;

sentences.zh: 會聞之，心慍懟。

translations.literal: Hui heard it; his heart was angry and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: when Hui heard the news, rage filled his heart.

sentences.zh: 九月，章武王宙奉燕方垂及成哀段后之喪葬於龍城宣平陵。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Prince Zhangwu Zhou conducted the mourning burial of Yan's late Chui and Empress Duan Cheng'ai at Xuanping Mausoleum in Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Prince Zhangwu Zhou escorted the remains of the late Murong Chui and Empress Duan Cheng'ai to burial at Xuanping Mausoleum in Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 寶詔宙悉高陽王隆參佐、部曲、家屬還中山，會違詔，多留部曲不遣。

translations.literal: Bao ordered Zhou to send all Gaoyang Wang Long's aides, personal forces, and families back to Zhongshan; Hui disobeyed the edict and kept many personal forces, not sending them.
translations.idiomatic: Bao ordered Zhou to send Gaoyang Wang Long's staff, troops, and families back to Zhongshan, but Hui defied the edict and kept much of Long's following with him.

sentences.zh: 宙年長屬尊，會每事陵侮之，見者皆知其有異志。

translations.literal: Zhou was older and of honored rank; Hui in every matter humiliated and insulted him; observers all knew he had rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was the elder and the more honored, yet Hui humiliated him at every turn, and all who saw it knew rebellion was brewing in his heart.

sentences.zh: 戊午，魏軍至陽曲，乘西山，臨晉陽，遣騎環城大噪而去。

translations.literal: Wuwu, Wei army reached Yangqu, mounted the western hills, overlooked Jinyang, sent cavalry to circle the city with great clamor and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the Wei army reached Yangqu, took the western hills above Jinyang, and sent horsemen to ride around the walls in a great clamor before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 燕遼西王農出戰，大敗，奔還晉陽，司馬慕輿嵩閉門拒之。

translations.literal: Yan Liaoxi Wang Nong went out to battle, was greatly defeated, fled back to Jinyang; Marshal Muyu Song closed the gates and refused him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong, Liaoxi Wang of Yan, rode out to fight and was routed. When he fled back to Jinyang, Marshal Muyu Song shut the gates against him.

sentences.zh: 農將妻子帥數千騎東走，魏中領將軍長孫肥追之，及於潞川，獲農妻子。

translations.literal: Nong led wife and children, commanding several thousand cavalry eastward; Wei Central Guard General Zhangsun Fei pursued, caught up at Luchuan, and captured Nong's wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Nong fled east with his wife, children, and a few thousand horsemen. Zhangsun Fei, Central Guard General of Wei, overtook him on the Luchuan and seized his family.

sentences.zh: 燕軍盡沒，農被創，獨與三騎逃歸中山。

translations.literal: Yan army was entirely destroyed; Nong was wounded; alone with three riders he escaped back to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's army was wiped out. Wounded, Nong escaped with only three riders back to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪遂取并州。

translations.literal: Wei King Gui then took Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wei King Gui then seized Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 初建台省，置刺史、太守、尚書郎以下官，悉用儒生為之。

translations.literal: First established the platform and secretariat offices; set up inspectors, administrators, Masters of Writing gentlemen and lower offices—all used Confucian scholars for them.
translations.idiomatic: He established the provincial and central bureaucracy, appointing inspectors, administrators, Masters of Writing, and lesser officials, and filled every post with Confucian-trained men.

sentences.zh: 士大夫詣軍門者，無少長，皆引入存慰，使人人盡言，少有才用，咸加擢敘。

translations.literal: Gentry and officials who came to the army gate, regardless of age, were all brought in and comforted; each was made to speak fully; those with even slight talent and use were all promoted and enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and officials who came to his camp, young or old, were received and questioned at length. Anyone who showed the least ability was promoted on the spot.

sentences.zh: 己未，遣輔國將軍奚收略地汾川，獲燕丹楊王買得及離石護軍高秀和。

translations.literal: Jiwei, sent General Who Supports the State Xi Shou to seize territory in Fen River valley; captured Yan Prince of Danyang Maide and Protective General of Lishi Gao Xiuhe.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei he sent Xi Shou, General Who Supports the State, to overrun the Fen valley and captured Maide, Prince of Danyang under Yan, and Gao Xiuhe, Protective General of Lishi.

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎張恂等為諸郡太守，招撫離散，勸課農桑。

translations.literal: Made Palace Attendant Zhang Xun and others administrators of various commanderies; summoned and comforted the scattered; urged agricultural and sericultural work.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zhang Xun, Palace Attendant, and others commandery administrators, gathered the displaced, and urged them back to farming and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 燕主寶聞魏軍將至，議於東堂。

translations.literal: Yan ruler Bao heard Wei army was about to arrive; deliberated at the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao learned that Wei forces were approaching, he held council in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 中山尹苻謨曰：「今魏軍眾強，千里遠鬥，乘勝氣銳。

translations.literal: Prefect of Zhongshan Fu Mo said: "Now Wei army is numerous and strong, fighting a thousand li from home, riding victory with sharp spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Mo, Prefect of Zhongshan, said, "Wei's army is huge and strong, fighting far from home yet riding a wave of victory.

sentences.zh: 若縱之使入平土，不可敵，宜杜險以拒之。」

translations.literal: If we let them enter level land, we cannot match them; we ought to block the passes and dangerous terrain to resist them."
translations.idiomatic: If we let them onto open ground we cannot stand against them. We should hold the mountain passes and keep them out."

sentences.zh: 中書令眭邃曰：「魏多騎兵，往來剽速，馬上繼糧，不過旬日。

translations.literal: Chief Secretary Suixuan said: "Wei has many cavalry, coming and going swift as robbers; grain carried on horseback lasts no more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretary Suixuan said, "Wei relies on cavalry that strikes and withdraws with terrifying speed. Grain carried on horseback lasts barely ten days.

sentences.zh: 宜令郡縣聚民千家為一堡，深溝高壘，清野以待之。

translations.literal: We ought to order commanderies and counties to gather people, a thousand households to one fort; deep moats and high ramparts; clear the countryside and wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: Order every commandery and county to gather the people into forts of a thousand households each, dig deep moats, raise high walls, and strip the countryside bare while we wait them out.

sentences.zh: 彼至無所掠，不過六旬，食盡自退。」

translations.literal: When they arrive with nothing to plunder, in no more than sixty days food exhausted they will withdraw of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: When they find nothing to loot, within sixty days their supplies will run out and they will withdraw on their own."

sentences.zh: 尚書封懿曰；

translations.literal: Master of Writing Feng Yi said:
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Feng Yi said,

sentences.zh: 「今魏兵數十萬，天下之勍敵也，民雖築堡，不足以自固，是聚兵及糧以資之也。

translations.literal: "Now Wei troops number several hundred thousand—the world's fierce enemy; though people build forts, it is not enough to secure themselves—this is gathering troops and grain to supply the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: "Wei now fields several hundred thousand men, the fiercest foe under Heaven. Even if the people build forts, they cannot hold them—it would only pile up soldiers and grain for the enemy to take.

sentences.zh: 且動搖民心，示之以弱。

translations.literal: Moreover it shakes the people's hearts and shows them weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, it would panic the people and advertise our weakness.

sentences.zh: 不如阻關拒戰，計之上也。」

translations.literal: Better to block passes and refuse battle—this is the highest plan."
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold the passes and fight—that is the wiser course."

sentences.zh: 趙王麟曰：「魏今乘勝氣銳，其鋒不可當，宜完守中山，待其弊而乘之。」

translations.literal: Zhao Wang Lin said: "Wei now rides victory with sharp spirit; its edge cannot be matched; we ought to complete defense of Zhongshan and wait for their exhaustion, then seize the moment."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wang Lin said, "Wei is riding a crest of victory and its edge cannot be met head-on. We should fortify Zhongshan and wait until they weaken, then strike."

sentences.zh: 於是修城積粟，為持久之備。

translations.literal: Thereupon they repaired walls and stored grain, making preparations for a prolonged stand.
translations.idiomatic: They repaired the walls, stockpiled grain, and prepared for a long siege.

sentences.zh: 命遼西王農出屯安喜，軍事動靜，悉以委麟。

translations.literal: Ordered Liaoxi Wang Nong to go out and encamp at Anxi; military movements and stillness were all entrusted to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong, Liaoxi Wang, was ordered to encamp at Anxi, and all military decisions were placed in Lin's hands.

sentences.zh: 帝嗜酒，流連內殿，醒治既少，外人罕得進見。

translations.literal: The emperor was fond of wine, lingered in the inner halls; sober governance was already scant; outsiders rarely gained audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was a drunkard who lingered in the inner palace. Sober governance grew rare, and outsiders seldom saw him.

sentences.zh: 張貴人寵冠後宮，後宮皆畏之。

translations.literal: Consort Zhang's favor crowned the inner palace; all the inner palace feared her.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhang's favor outshone every woman in the palace, and the whole inner household feared her.

sentences.zh: 庚申，帝與後宮宴，妓樂盡侍；

translations.literal: Gengshen, the emperor feasted with the inner palace; courtesans and musicians all attended;
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the emperor held a banquet with the inner palace, every musician and dancer in attendance;

sentences.zh: 時貴人年近三十，帝戲之曰：「汝以年亦當廢矣，吾意更屬少者。」

translations.literal: At the time the consort was nearly thirty; the emperor teased her: "With your age you too ought to be set aside; my mind turns rather to younger ones."
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhang was nearly thirty. The emperor joked, "At your age you ought to be cast off too—I have my eye on someone younger."

sentences.zh: 貴人潛怒，向夕，帝醉，寢於清暑殿，貴人遍飲宦者酒，散遣之，使婢以被蒙帝面，弒之，重賂左右，云「因魘暴崩」。

translations.literal: The consort secretly raged; toward evening the emperor was drunk, slept in the Clear Summer Hall; the consort made all eunuchs drink wine and dispersed them; had a maid cover the emperor's face with a quilt and assassinate him; heavily bribed attendants, declaring "died suddenly in nightmare."
translations.idiomatic: “She hid her fury. That evening, when the emperor was drunk and asleep in the Clear Summer Hall, she plied the eunuchs with wine and sent them away, then had a maid smother his face with a quilt and kill him. She bribed those around her heavily and had it announced that he had died suddenly in his sleep.”

sentences.zh: 時太子闇弱，會稽王道子昏荒，遂不復推問。

translations.literal: At the time the crown prince was dim and weak; Prince of Kuaiji Daozi was muddled and dissolute; thus no further investigation was pursued.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was feeble-minded, and Prince of Kuaiji Daozi was lost in debauchery, so no one pressed the matter further.

sentences.zh: 王國寶夜叩禁門，欲入為遺詔，侍中王爽拒之，曰：「大行晏駕，皇太子未至，敢入者斬！」

translations.literal: Wang Guobao by night knocked at the forbidden gate, wishing to enter to draft the final edict; Palace Attendant Wang Shuang refused him, saying: "The late emperor has departed; the crown prince has not arrived—whoever dares enter, beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: That night Wang Guobao hammered on the forbidden gate, trying to enter and draft a deathbed edict. Palace Attendant Wang Shuang barred him. "The late emperor has just died and the crown prince has not yet arrived," he said. "Anyone who enters now dies!"

sentences.zh: 國寶乃止。

translations.literal: Guobao then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 爽，恭之弟也。

translations.literal: Shuang was Gong's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was a younger brother of Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，太子即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: Xinyou, crown prince took the emperor's throne; great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the crown prince ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，有司奏：「會稽王道子宜進位太傅、揚州牧，假黃鉞。」

translations.literal: Guihai, the relevant offices memorialized: "Prince of Kuaiji Daozi ought to advance to Grand Tutor, Governor of Yang Province, with provisional yellow axe."
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the responsible offices memorialized that Prince of Kuaiji Daozi should be promoted to Grand Tutor and Governor of Yang Province and granted the yellow battle-axe."

sentences.zh: 詔內外眾事動靜咨之。

translations.literal: An edict: on all matters within and without, movement and stillness, consult him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed that all affairs of state, great and small, were to be referred to him.

sentences.zh: 安帝幼而不慧，口不能言，至於寒暑饑飽亦不能辨，飲食寢興皆非己出。

translations.literal: Emperor An was young and without intelligence; mouth could not speak; as for cold, heat, hunger, and fullness he also could not distinguish; eating, drinking, sleeping, and rising were none from himself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An was a child without wit. He could not speak, could not tell cold from heat or hunger from fullness, and never chose for himself when to eat, sleep, or rise.

sentences.zh: 母弟琅邪王德文，性恭謹，常侍左右，為之節適，始得其宜。

translations.literal: Younger brother by the same mother, Prince of Langya Dewen, nature respectful and careful, constantly attended at his side, regulated for him what was fitting; only then obtained what was proper.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother, Prince of Langya Dewen, was gentle and dutiful. He stayed constantly at the emperor's side, regulating every need, and only then did life proceed as it should.

sentences.zh: 初，王國寶黨附會稽王道子，驕縱不法，屢為御史中丞褚粲所糾。

translations.literal: Initially, Wang Guobao clung to Prince of Kuaiji Daozi's faction, arrogant and unrestrained against law; repeatedly was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Chu Can.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Guobao had attached himself to Prince of Kuaiji Daozi, growing arrogant and lawless until Censor-in-Chief Chu Can impeached him again and again.

sentences.zh: 國寶起齋，侔清暑殿，孝武帝甚惡之；

translations.literal: Guobao built a hall rivaling the Clear Summer Hall; Emperor Xiaowu greatly hated it;
translations.idiomatic: Guobao built a private hall to rival the Clear Summer Palace, which Emperor Xiaowu deeply resented;

sentences.zh: 國寶懼，遂更求媚於帝而疏道子，帝復寵暱之。

translations.literal: Guobao feared; then changed to seek favor with the emperor and kept distance from Daozi; the emperor again favored and drew him close.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Guobao turned to flatter the emperor and distanced himself from Daozi, and the emperor once again showered him with favor.

sentences.zh: 道子大怒，嘗於內省面責國寶，以劍擲之，舊好盡矣。

translations.literal: Daozi greatly raged; once in the inner office face to face rebuked Guobao and threw a sword at him; old friendship was entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi flew into a rage, once rebuked Guobao to his face in the inner office, and even hurled a sword at him. Their old friendship was finished.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，國寶復事道子，與王緒共為邪諂。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Guobao again served Daozi; with Wang Xu jointly practiced wicked flattery.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death, Guobao returned to Daozi's service and, with Wang Xu, practiced their corrupt flattery together.

sentences.zh: 道子更惑之，倚為心腹，遂參管朝權，威震內外，並為時之所疾。

translations.literal: Daozi was further deluded by them, relied on them as trusted intimates; then jointly managed court power; authority shook inside and outside; both were what the age resented.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi, deceived anew, leaned on them as his inner circle. They shared control of court power, their sway terrifying inside and outside the palace, and the age despised them both.

sentences.zh: 王恭入赴山陵，每正色直言，道子深憚之。

translations.literal: Wang Gong entered to attend the imperial tomb; each time with stern countenance spoke straight; Daozi deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong came to attend the imperial burial, and each time he spoke plainly with a stern face Daozi feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 恭罷朝，歎曰：「榱棟雖新，便有黍離之歎！」
