translations.literal: Gong after court sighed: "Though rafters and beams are new, already there is the sigh of Shu Li!"
translations.idiomatic: After court Gong sighed, "The palace beams are still new, yet already I hear the lament of fallen dynasties!"

sentences.zh: 緒說國寶，因恭入朝，勸相王伏兵殺之，國寶不許。

translations.literal: Xu persuaded Guobao: when Gong entered court, urge the Prince to set hidden troops to kill him; Guobao did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Xu urged Guobao that when Gong next came to court, the Prince should set an ambush and kill him. Guobao refused.

sentences.zh: 道子欲輯和內外，乃深布腹心於恭，冀除舊惡；

translations.literal: Daozi wished to harmonize inside and outside; then deeply spread trusted hearts toward Gong, hoping to remove old enmity;
translations.idiomatic: Daozi wanted to reconcile with the court at large and opened his heart to Gong, hoping to bury old grievances;

sentences.zh: 而恭每言及時政，輒厲聲色。

translations.literal: but Gong whenever he spoke of current affairs, immediately raised harsh voice and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: but whenever Gong spoke of public affairs his voice turned harsh and his face hard.

sentences.zh: 道子知恭不可和協，遂有相圖之志。

translations.literal: Daozi knew Gong could not be reconciled; then had the will to plot against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi saw that Gong would not be reconciled, and began to think of removing him.

sentences.zh: 或勸恭因入朝以兵誅國寶，恭以豫州刺史庾楷士馬甚盛，黨於國寶，憚之，不敢發。

translations.literal: Some urged Gong that on entering court he use troops to execute Guobao; Gong because Inspector of Yu Province Yu Kai's soldiers and horses were very strong and allied with Guobao, feared this, and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Gong to use his troops at the next court audience to kill Guobao, but Yu Kai, Inspector of Yu Province, commanded a powerful force allied with Guobao, and Gong feared him and held back.

sentences.zh: 王珣謂恭曰：「國寶雖終為禍亂，要之罪逆未彰，今遽先事而安，必大失朝野之望。

translations.literal: Wang Xun said to Gong: "Guobao though in the end will become calamity and disorder, in sum his crimes and rebellion are not yet manifest; now hastily to act first and find peace is sure greatly to lose court and countryside's hope.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun told Gong, "Guobao will bring disaster in the end, but his crimes are not yet plain. If you strike first now, you will lose the trust of court and country alike.

sentences.zh: 況擁強兵竊發於京輦，誰謂非逆！

translations.literal: Moreover, holding strong troops and secretly launching at the capital region—who would say it is not rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: And if you mobilize armed men and strike secretly in the capital itself, who will not call that treason?

sentences.zh: 國寶若遂不改，惡布天下，然後順眾心以除之，亦無憂不濟也。」

translations.literal: If Guobao then does not reform, evil spreads through all under Heaven; afterward follow the multitude's hearts to remove him—also no worry it will not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: If Guobao goes on unchanged until his wickedness is known everywhere, then you may remove him with the people's backing—and you need not fear failure."

sentences.zh: 恭乃止。

translations.literal: Gong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gong held his hand.

sentences.zh: 既而謂珣曰：「比來視君一似胡廣」。

translations.literal: Afterward he said to Xun: "Lately in viewing you, you seem quite like Hu Guang."
translations.idiomatic: Later he told Xun, "These days you remind me of Hu Guang."

sentences.zh: 珣曰：「王陵廷爭，陳平慎默，但問歲晏何如耳！」

translations.literal: Xun said: "Wang Ling contested at court; Chen Ping was careful and silent, only asking how the year's end harvest was!"
translations.idiomatic: Xun replied, "Wang Ling spoke boldly in open court, while Chen Ping held his tongue—he only asked how the harvest was faring!"

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲申，葬孝武帝於隆平陵。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jia-shen, buried Emperor Xiaowu at Longping Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day jia-shen, Emperor Xiaowu was interred at Longping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 王恭還鎮，將行，謂道子曰：「主上諒暗，塚宰之任，伊、周所難，願大王親萬幾，納直言。

translations.literal: Wang Gong returned to his post, about to depart, said to Daozi: "The lord is in mourning obscurity; the burden of chief minister—even Yi and Zhou found it hard; I hope the great prince will personally attend to the myriad affairs and accept direct speech.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Gong returned to his command and was about to leave, he told Daozi, "The Emperor is still in mourning; the regent's burden is one even Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou found daunting. I hope Your Highness will personally oversee state affairs and heed frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 放鄭聲，遠佞人。」

translations.literal: Dismiss Zheng music, keep flatterers at a distance."
translations.idiomatic: Put aside licentious music and keep sycophants at arm's length."

sentences.zh: 國寶等愈懼。

translations.literal: Guobao and the others grew ever more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao and his faction grew still more alarmed.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪使冠軍將軍代人於栗磾、寧朔將軍公孫蘭帥步騎二萬，潛自晉陽開韓信故道。

translations.literal: Wei Wang Gui sent Champion General Yu Libi of Dai and Ningshuo General Gongsun Lan to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry, secretly opening Han Xin's old route from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wang Gui dispatched Champion General Yu Libi of Dai and Ningshuo General Gongsun Lan with twenty thousand foot and horse, who secretly reopened Han Xin's old road from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 己酉，珪自井陘趨中山。

translations.literal: Day ji-you, Gui from Jingxing hastened toward Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ji-you, Gui marched from Jingxing toward Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 李先降魏，珪以為征東左長史。

translations.literal: Li Xian surrendered to Wei; Gui made him Left Chief Clerk of the Eastern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian surrendered to Wei, and Gui appointed him Left Chief Clerk of the Eastern Campaign.

sentences.zh: 西秦涼州牧軻彈與秦州牧益州不平，軻彈奔涼。

translations.literal: Western Qin: Liangzhou Governor Ke Tan and Qinzhou Governor Yizhou were at odds; Ke Tan fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In Western Qin, Ke Tan, Governor of Liangzhou, fell out with Yizhou, Governor of Qinzhou, and Ke Tan fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪進攻常山，拔之，獲太守苟延，自常山以東，守宰或走或降，諸郡縣皆附於魏，惟中山、鄴、信都三城為燕守。

translations.literal: Wei Wang Gui advanced to attack Changshan, took it, captured Prefect Gou Yan; east of Changshan, defending officials either fled or surrendered; all commanderies and counties submitted to Wei; only Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu—three cities—still held for Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wang Gui attacked Changshan, captured it, and took its prefect Gou Yan. East of Changshan, local officials either fled or surrendered, and commanderies and counties everywhere submitted to Wei; only Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu still held out for Yan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，珪命東平公儀將五萬騎攻鄴，冠軍將軍王建、左將軍李栗攻信都。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Gui ordered Dongping Duke Yi to lead fifty thousand cavalry to attack Ye; Champion General Wang Jian and Left General Li Li to attack Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Gui ordered Dongping Duke Yi to lead fifty thousand horsemen against Ye, while Champion General Wang Jian and Left General Li Li attacked Xindu.

sentences.zh: 戊午，珪進軍中山；

translations.literal: Day wu-wu, Gui advanced his army to Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: On the day wu-wu, Gui marched on Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 己未，攻之。

translations.literal: Day ji-wei, attacked it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ji-wei, he assaulted the city.

sentences.zh: 燕高陽王隆守南郭，帥眾力戰，自旦至晡，殺傷數千人，魏兵乃退。

translations.literal: Yan Prince of Gaoyang Long defended the south gate, led the host in fierce battle from dawn to mid-afternoon, killed and wounded several thousand; Wei troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's Prince of Gaoyang, Long, held the south gate and fought hard from dawn until mid-afternoon, killing and wounding several thousand men before the Wei army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 珪謂諸將曰：「中山城固，寶必不肯出戰。

translations.literal: Gui told the generals: "Zhongshan city is strong; Bao will surely refuse to come out and fight.
translations.idiomatic: Gui told his generals, "Zhongshan is a strong city, and Bao will surely refuse to give battle.

sentences.zh: 急攻則傷士，久圍則費糧，不如先取鄴、信都，然後圖之。」

translations.literal: Urgent attack then harms soldiers; long siege then wastes grain; better first take Ye and Xindu, afterward plan against it."
translations.idiomatic: A hasty assault will cost us men; a long siege will drain our grain. Better to take Ye and Xindu first, then turn back to deal with it."

sentences.zh: 丁卯，珪引兵而南。

translations.literal: Day ding-mao, Gui led troops southward.
translations.idiomatic: On the day ding-mao, Gui withdrew his army and marched south.

sentences.zh: 章武王寅自龍城還，聞有魏寇，馳入薊，與鎮北將軍陽城王蘭乘城固守。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhangwu Yin returned from Longcheng, heard there were Wei raiders, raced into Ji, with Northern Garrison General Prince of Yangcheng Lan mounted the walls and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhangwu Yin had just returned from Longcheng when he heard of Wei raiders; he galloped into Ji and, with Northern Garrison General Prince of Yangcheng Lan, manned the walls and held fast.

sentences.zh: 蘭，垂之從弟也。

translations.literal: Lan was Chui's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Lan was a younger cousin of Chui.

sentences.zh: 魏別將石河頭攻之，不克，退屯漁陽。

translations.literal: Wei detached general Shi Hetou attacked it, could not take it, withdrew and encamped at Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hetou, a detached Wei general, attacked the city but failed to take it and withdrew to encamp at Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 珪軍於魯口，博陵太守申永奔河南，高陽太守崔宏奔海渚。

translations.literal: Gui encamped at Lukou; Boling Prefect Shen Yong fled to Henan; Gaoyang Prefect Cui Hong fled to the sea isles.
translations.idiomatic: Gui encamped at Lukou. Boling Prefect Shen Yong fled south to Henan, and Gaoyang Prefect Cui Hong fled to the coastal isles.

sentences.zh: 珪素聞宏名，遣吏追求，獲之，以為黃門侍郎，與給事黃門侍郎張袞對掌機要，創立制度。

translations.literal: Gui had long heard of Hong's fame, sent officers to pursue and capture him, made him Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, paired with Secretary Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zhang Gun to jointly manage state secrets, and established institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had long known Hong by reputation and sent officers to hunt him down. Once captured, Hong was made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and, together with Secretary Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zhang Gun, shared control of confidential affairs and helped establish the new administrative order.

sentences.zh: 博陵令屈遵降魏，珪為中書令，出納號令，兼總文誥。

translations.literal: Boling Magistrate Qu Zun surrendered to Wei; Gui made him Director of the Secretariat, issuing and receiving orders, also overseeing all written edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Boling Magistrate Qu Zun surrendered to Wei, and Gui appointed him Director of the Secretariat, charged with issuing and receiving orders and overseeing all written proclamations.

sentences.zh: 燕范陽王德使南安王青等夜擊魏軍於鄴下，破之，魏軍退屯新城。

translations.literal: Yan Prince of Fanyang De sent Prince of Nan'an Qing and others to attack the Wei army at Ye by night, defeated them; the Wei army withdrew and encamped at Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's Prince of Fanyang, De, sent Prince of Nan'an Qing and others to strike the Wei army below Ye by night. They routed the enemy, and the Wei forces withdrew to encamp at Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 青等請追擊之，別駕韓言卓曰：「古人先計而後戰。

translations.literal: Qing and the others asked to pursue and attack; Administrator Han Yanzhuo said: "The ancients planned first and fought afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and the others asked to pursue, but Administrator Han Yanzhuo said, "The ancients planned first and fought only afterward.

sentences.zh: 魏軍不可擊者四：懸軍遠客，利在野戰，一也；

translations.literal: Reasons the Wei army must not be attacked are four: an army suspended far from home, advantage lies in field battle—first;
translations.idiomatic: There are four reasons not to attack the Wei army: they are a force far from home with everything to gain from open battle—first;

sentences.zh: 深入近畿，頓兵死地，二也；

translations.literal: Deep penetration near the capital region, troops halted in deadly ground—second;
translations.idiomatic: they have pushed deep toward the capital and will stand their ground as if on death ground—second;

sentences.zh: 前鋒既敗，後陣方固，三也；

translations.literal: The vanguard has already been defeated, the rear ranks are now firm—third;
translations.idiomatic: their vanguard has already been beaten, but their rear ranks are now steady—third;

sentences.zh: 彼眾我寡，四也。

translations.literal: They are many, we are few—fourth.
translations.idiomatic: they outnumber us—fourth.

sentences.zh: 官軍不宜動者三：自戰其地，一也；

translations.literal: Reasons the official army should not move are three: fighting on one's own ground—first;
translations.idiomatic: There are three reasons our own army should not stir: we would be fighting on our own soil—first;

sentences.zh: 動而不勝，眾心難固，二也；

translations.literal: Move and not win, the multitude's hearts are hard to keep firm—second;
translations.idiomatic: if we move and fail to win, morale will be hard to hold—second;

sentences.zh: 城隍未修，敵來無備，三也。

translations.literal: City walls and moat not yet repaired, when the enemy comes there is no defense—third.
translations.idiomatic: our walls and moat are not yet repaired, so we are unprepared if the enemy returns—third.

sentences.zh: 今魏無資糧，不如深壘固軍以老之。」

translations.literal: Now Wei has no supplies; better to fortify deeply, hold the army firm, and wear them down."
translations.idiomatic: Wei now lacks provisions. Better to entrench deeply, hold our lines, and wear them down."

sentences.zh: 德從之，召青還。

translations.literal: De followed this, recalled Qing.
translations.idiomatic: De agreed, and recalled Qing.

sentences.zh: 青，詳之兄也。

translations.literal: Qing was Xiang's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was the elder brother of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏遼西公賀賴盧帥騎二萬會東平公議攻鄴。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Wei Liaoxi Duke Helu led twenty thousand cavalry to join Dongping Duke Yi in planning an attack on Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Wei's Liaoxi Duke Helu led twenty thousand horsemen to join Dongping Duke Yi in planning an assault on Ye.

sentences.zh: 賴盧，訥之弟也。

translations.literal: Helu was Ne's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Helu was the younger brother of Ne.

sentences.zh: 魏別部大人沒根有膽勇，魏王珪惡之。

translations.literal: Wei detached tribal chief Meigen had courage and bravery; Wei Wang Gui disliked him.
translations.idiomatic: Meigen, a detached tribal chieftain of Wei, was bold and brave, and Wei Wang Gui disliked him.

sentences.zh: 沒根懼誅，己丑，將親兵數十人降燕，燕主寶以為鎮東大將軍，封雁門公。

translations.literal: Meigen feared execution; day ji-chou, led several dozen personal troops to surrender to Yan; Yan ruler Bao made him Grand General Who Guards the East, enfeoffed as Duke of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing execution, Meigen on the day ji-chou brought several dozen personal followers and surrendered to Yan. Yan's ruler Bao made him Grand General Who Guards the East and enfeoffed him as Duke of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 沒根求還襲魏，寶難與重兵，給百餘騎。

translations.literal: Meigen asked to return and raid Wei; Bao was reluctant to give him a large force, gave a bit over a hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Meigen asked to go back and strike Wei, but Bao was unwilling to give him a large force and allotted him only a little over a hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 沒根效其號令，夜入魏營，至中仗，珪乃覺之，狼狽驚走；

translations.literal: Meigen imitated their signals, entered the Wei camp by night, reached the middle watch before Gui realized it; he fled in panic and disarray;
translations.idiomatic: Meigen copied their camp signals and entered the Wei encampment by night. Not until the middle watch did Gui realize what had happened, and he fled in panic and disorder;

sentences.zh: 沒根以所從人少，不能壞其大眾，多獲首虜而還。

translations.literal: Meigen because those who followed him were few could not break their main force, but captured many heads and prisoners and returned.
translations.idiomatic: With too few men at his back, Meigen could not break the main Wei force, but he took many heads and captives and returned.

sentences.zh: 楊盛遣使來請命。

translations.literal: Yang Sheng sent envoys to request imperial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng sent envoys to request an imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 詔拜盛鎮南將軍、仇池公。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Sheng General Who Guards the South, Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Sheng General Who Guards the South and Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 盛表苻宣為平北將軍。

translations.literal: Sheng recommended Fu Xuan as General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng recommended Fu Xuan for appointment as General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 是歲，越質詰歸帥戶二萬叛西秦降於秦，秦人處之成紀，拜鎮西將軍、平襄公。

translations.literal: That year, Yue Zhi Gui led twenty thousand households in rebellion against Western Qin and surrendered to Qin; Qin people settled them at Chengji, appointed him General Who Guards the West, Duke of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yue Zhi Gui led twenty thousand households in revolt against Western Qin and surrendered to Qin. The Qin settled them at Chengji and appointed him General Who Guards the West and Duke of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 秦隴西王碩德攻姜乳於上邽，乳帥眾降。

translations.literal: Qin Prince of Longxi Shuode attacked Jiang Ru at Shanggui; Ru led his forces in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's Prince of Longxi, Shuode, attacked Jiang Ru at Shanggui, and Ru surrendered with his followers.

sentences.zh: 秦以碩德為秦州牧，鎮上邽；

translations.literal: Qin made Shuode Governor of Qinzhou, stationed at Shanggui;
translations.idiomatic: Qin appointed Shuode Governor of Qinzhou and stationed him at Shanggui;

sentences.zh: 征乳為尚書。

translations.literal: Summoned Ru as Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Ru was summoned to serve as Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 強熙、權千成帥眾三萬共圍上邽，碩德擊破之，熙奔仇池，遂來奔。

translations.literal: Qiang Xi and Quan Qiancheng led thirty thousand troops jointly to besiege Shanggui; Shuode defeated them; Xi fled to Chouchi, then came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Xi and Quan Qiancheng jointly led thirty thousand men to besiege Shanggui, but Shuode routed them. Xi fled to Chouchi and then came over to surrender.

sentences.zh: 碩德西去千成於略陽，千成降。

translations.literal: Shuode went west against Qiancheng at Lueyang; Qiancheng surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shuode marched west against Qiancheng at Lueyang, and Qiancheng surrendered.

sentences.zh: 西燕既亡，其所署河東太守柳恭等各擁兵自守。

translations.literal: Western Yan having perished, its appointed Hedong Prefect Liu Gong and others each held troops and defended themselves.
translations.idiomatic: After Western Yan fell, Liu Gong, whom it had appointed Prefect of Hedong, and others each kept armed forces and held out on their own.

sentences.zh: 秦主興遣晉王緒攻之，恭等臨河拒守，緒不得濟。

translations.literal: Qin ruler Xing sent Prince of Jin Xu to attack them; Gong and others faced the river and resisted; Xu could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's ruler Xing sent Prince of Jin Xu to attack them, but Gong and the others held the riverbank and blocked him, and Xu could not get across.

sentences.zh: 初，永嘉之亂，汾陰薛氏聚其族黨，阻河自固，不仕劉、石。

translations.literal: Initially, during the Yongjia turmoil, the Xue clan of Fenyin gathered their kinsmen and partisans, blocked the river and held firm, and did not serve Liu or Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Yongjia upheaval, the Xue clan of Fenyin gathered their kin and allies, fortified themselves behind the river, and refused to serve the Liu or Shi regimes.

sentences.zh: 及苻氏興，乃以禮聘薛強，拜鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: When the Fu clan rose, then with courtesy invited Xue Qiang, appointed him General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fu clan came to power, they courteously invited Xue Qiang out and appointed him General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 強引秦兵自龍門濟，遂入蒲阪，恭等皆降。

translations.literal: Qiang led Qin troops across at Longmen, then entered Puban; Gong and the others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang guided Qin troops across at Longmen, entered Puban, and Gong and the others all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 興以緒為并、冀二州牧，鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: Xing made Xu Governor of Bing and Ji provinces, stationed at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Xing appointed Xu Governor of Bing and Ji provinces and stationed him at Puban.
